disclaimer.normal_residence: Exchange almost always requires that you were normally resident in the issuing country when (and often while) you held the licence, and that you are resident in the destination when you exchange. EU law defines normal residence as living in a place for at least 185 days in each calendar year (Directive 2006/126/EC Art. 12). Several national authorities (e.g. Netherlands RDW) restate the same 185-day rule for non-EU licences. A licence obtained without meeting that condition is often void in the destination.
disclaimer.scope: Lawful exchange conditions only. This is not a guide to licence tourism, and the one-licence rule means there is no stacking to be done: you end up holding exactly one, from where you reside.
disclaimer.coverage: 45 destinations and 909 origin rows: the fourteen seeded lists plus four regional research batches (Americas, Europe, Asia, Gulf). THIRTEEN DESTINATIONS ARE SUB-NATIONAL and carry no ISO at all — Alberta, British Columbia and Ontario, and the US states of Connecticut, Delaware, Georgia, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Oregon, Vermont, Virginia and Wisconsin. There is no Canadian or US federal driving licence and no federal exchange list, so there is NO Canada row and NO United States row, and neither federation is painted as a destination: read the province or the state, not the flag. The same problem arrives on the origin side under the Swiss bilaterals, where the counterparty ITSELF is sub-national in eight cases — seven Canadian provinces and the US state of Louisiana — and those rows are listed in the table but are DELIBERATELY NOT PAINTED on the map, because Canada and the United States have no Swiss licence treaty at federal level. Japan is the sharpest case of a list that means less than it looks: its published 29-country list waives only the ADMINISTRATIVE knowledge and skills confirmations, while 施行令 art. 34-4(2) already waives the statutory tests for any foreign Class 1 licence — so Japan exchanges from everywhere, and that list is not the list of countries it exchanges from. Dubai is EMIRATE-LEVEL, not federal, and is the one list carrying a per-origin NATIONALITY GATE: 35 of its 60 origins accept the licence only from that country's own nationals. Türkiye's six months is the opposite clock from everyone else's — a grace period from the date of entry after which exchange becomes compulsory, not a deadline after which the right lapses. Where no nationality rule, no test requirement and no window is recorded, none was published: NULL MEANS NOT RECORDED, never "not required" and never "open to all". EU/EEA mutual recognition is not expanded as third-country annex rows anywhere in this corpus.
disclaimer.what_a_licence_evidences: A driving licence is best read as a RESIDENCE ARTEFACT, not a collectible. Under Directive 2006/126/EC the three rules lock together: issuance requires normal residence in the issuing state (art. 7(1)(e)); "No person may hold more than one driving licence" and a state "shall refuse to issue a licence where it establishes that the applicant already holds" one, verifying with other Member States through the EU driving licence network (art. 7(5)(a)-(d)); and on exchange the original is surrendered and the swap is recorded on the new licence (art. 11(6)). So the licence you hold is single, exclusive and anchored to where you actually live, which is why in practice it is widely accepted as evidence of address. That exclusivity is the point of this layer, not a limitation of it: the exchange network shows which residence histories convert into which documents.

SUB-NATIONAL PARTNERS: seven Canadian provinces and the US state of Louisiana concluded these instruments themselves. No Swiss-Canada or Swiss-USA federal licence treaty exists in the series, so those eight rows carry no country ISO and neither federation is painted on the map.

The six Canadian letter-exchanges quote the Switzerland-to-province leg and are expressly conditional on Swiss reciprocity: the instrument is bilateral, but the inbound examination treatment is not established from the cited text and is left unrecorded.

Where an instrument waives only the «examen de conduite» (Luxembourg, Spain), the practical test is recorded as waived and the theory field is left unrecorded rather than assumed. Exchange still runs through the Swiss residence and licensing procedure.

entries.note: SR 0.741.531.917.2 (exchange of notes, 1971): a corresponding licence «sans avoir à subir un examen». An exam is reserved for doubt as to fitness, circumvention of competence rules, or professional transport. Extends to Liechtenstein by mandate.

SR 0.741.531.937.2 (exchange of notes, 1980): recognition for one year from entry, then exchange without examination after a year's stay unbroken by three consecutive months away. Extends to Liechtenstein by mandate.

SR 0.741.531.941.8 (exchange of notes, 1971): recognition for one year, then exchange «sans avoir à subir un examen». Professional drivers may always be required to sit a driving test. Extends to Liechtenstein by mandate.

SR 0.741.531.945.4 (accord of 2021-05-13, in force 2021-06-12): «Chaque Partie reconnaît, aux fins de l'échange, les permis de conduire en cours de validité» — exchange, and recognition only for its purposes. SR 0.741.531.951.4 (accord of 2015-06-18): art. 2 recognition, art. 4(2) «La nouvelle autorité compétente délivre le permis de conduire sans examen» on change of domicile. Supersedes the 1978 and 1954 notes filed under the same SR number.

SR 0.741.531.951.8 (arrangement of 1973-02-15; the Swiss party is the Federal Department of Justice and Police, not the Confederation): art. 1 recognition, art. 2 headed «Renonciation à l'examen de conduire». SR 0.741.531.933.2 (exchange of notes, 1998): exchange for an equivalent licence on establishing normal residence «sans devoir se soumettre à un examen de conduite». destinations.name: United Arab Emirates — Dubai (RTA)
destinations.instrument: RTA service "Apply for a New Driving Licence or a New Category Based on Exchanging Licences", serviceId=121 ("Other Countries" variant), published service card; page states "Updated on: 22-July-2026". The sibling serviceId=122 is the separate Singapore variant.
notes: AUTHORITY IS EMIRATE-LEVEL. This row is Dubai's RTA list and nothing else. UAE driving licences are issued by each emirate's traffic authority, so the 60-origin annex here is not a federal instrument and must not be presented as one. The federal Ministry of Interior page that u.ae links for this service (https://moi.gov.ae/en/eservices/replacement.foreign.license.322.aspx) sits behind an F5 JavaScript/CAPTCHA gate and returns 311 bytes of challenge text to a plain fetch, so the federal list could not be read and is NOT asserted here. Abu Dhabi routes its equivalent service ("Replacement of Driving License of Another Countries") through TAMM, which serves a 4.6 KB SPA shell for every path, so Abu Dhabi Police's list could not be read either. ICP (icp.gov.ae) publishes no driving-licence service at all — it covers identity, nationality, customs and ports — so treating ICP as the federal licence-exchange authority would be wrong.

TEST FIELDS, AND WHY false RATHER THAN null. RTA publishes Service Requirements per service type on this page. For "Exchange Licence - Resident with Dubai visa" they are: "Valid Emirates ID", "Valid electronic eye test", "Original Driving Licence issued in the exception country" — no test. For "Exchange Licence - Holder of a Licence from an exception country different from my nationality" they are: "Knowledge Test results", "Road Test results", plus documents. The Steps for the exchange list submit / verify / open traffic file / pay / receive, with no test step; the sibling Singapore service (serviceId=122) by contrast lists "Book an appointment for the Knowledge Test", "Pass the Knowledge Test" and "Knowledge Test results". The false values therefore rest on RTA stating where a test applies and stating a different requirement set where it does not — not on silence. A reviewer who reads that contrast as insufficient should downgrade all 60 entries to null; the basis is recorded here so that judgement can be made rather than inherited.

SURRENDER VARIES BY ORIGIN and is carried per entry, from RTA's column "The Foreign Licence Must be Withdrawn (yes/no)". It is "Yes" for Albania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Greece, Hong Kong (no), Hungary, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia and Ukraine, and "Yes, from all GCC nationalities only" for the five GCC origins. RTA separately states of the GCC: "If you're a GCC national, your GCC Driving Licence must be valid to replace it, and you must surrender it."

NATIONALITY GATE. RTA's table has a "Nationality" column with three values: "All countries" (17 origins — the licence alone qualifies), "Nationals only" (38 origins — you must hold the nationality of the issuing country) and "All exception countries" (the five GCC states). This is the sharpest planning fact in the row and is why a German licence held by an Indian national exchanges while a Portuguese one held by the same person does not. destinations.name: Italy
destinations.instrument: Accordi di reciprocità per la conversione delle patenti di guida estere (art. 136 Codice della Strada, D.Lgs. 285/1992); condizioni di decadenza fissate dalla circolare prot. 31762 del 24 ottobre 2023
notes: THE CONVERSION CONDITION, IN THE MINISTRY'S OWN WORDS: "Ciò è possibile se lo Stato che ha rilasciato l'abilitazione alla guida ha sottoscritto accordi di reciprocità con l'Italia." and "La conversione è possibile, senza altre prove o esami, solo se" — which is why every listed origin is recorded with no theory and no practical test.

THE WINDOW VARIES BY ORIGIN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS ON THE ROWS AND NOT HERE. Per circolare prot. 31762 del 24 ottobre 2023 there are three regimes, and only two of them are deadlines. (1) FOUR YEARS from taking up residence for Albania, Argentina, Switzerland and Ukraine, after which the application is REFUSED OUTRIGHT with no re-examination available. (2) SIX YEARS on the same refused-outright terms for Andorra, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Kosovo, Israel, the United Kingdom (with Gibraltar, Guernsey, the Isle of Man and Jersey), Serbia, Tunisia, Türkiye, Morocco and Moldova. (3) For every other listed state there is NO deadline: after six years of residence the Italian licence is still issued, but is immediately subject to a revisione under art. 128 Codice della Strada. Rows in group (3) therefore carry no exchange_deadline_months at all — recording 72 there would tell a reader the right lapses when the ministry says it does not.

RESTRICTED CATEGORY — FOUR ROWS THAT ARE NOT A GENERAL ARRANGEMENT. Canada, Chile, the United States and Zambia sit under the separate heading "Stati esteri che rilasciano patenti convertibili in Italia solo ad alcune categorie di cittadini": diplomatic and consular staff and their families, and in Zambia's case citizens on government mission. They are carried because they are genuinely part of the annex, and they are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the agreement's beneficiaries so that no map paints Canada, Chile, the United States or Zambia as holding a general conversion arrangement with Italy.

The original is surrendered: where a revisione is failed the Italian licence is revoked and the converted foreign licence cannot be returned, because it has been sent back to the issuing authority. A licence itself obtained by converting another foreign licence that is not convertible in Italy cannot be converted ("Non possono essere convertite patenti estere ottenute per conversione di altra patente estera non convertibile in Italia.").

A non-EU/EEA licence may be used in Italy for one year from acquisition of residence; after that year it must be converted to keep driving. The foreign licence must have been obtained BEFORE Italian residence was acquired. A medical certificate is required.
EU/EEA mutual recognition under Directive 2006/126/EC is deliberately not expanded here. Ministry page last modified 13/07/2026.

destinations.name: Norway
destinations.instrument: Statens vegvesen — Innbytte av førerkort fra land utenfor EU/EØS (national exchange scheme; the eligible origins are enumerated by the authority, not by treaty)
notes: A CLOSED ANNEX WITH THREE DIFFERENT OUTCOMES, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE ROWS. Statens vegvesen: "Du kan få norsk førerkort hvis du har førerkort fra et av de landene utenfor EU/EØS som vi har nevnt her" — a licence from an unlisted non-EU/EEA country cannot be exchanged at all. Inside the annex the outcomes differ sharply: Australia, Canada, Israel, Monaco, New Zealand, San Marino, South Korea and the United States sit BOTH the theory test and the practical driving test after the application is granted; the United Kingdom and Switzerland are treated exactly as EEA licences and sit neither; Japan converts class B only, with no test, but within twelve months of taking up fast bopel; Greenland converts class B only and requires a practical driving test. A country list on its own cannot say this, which is why the test flags are per row.

No single deadline applies, so none is recorded at destination level: there is no deadline at all for the eight-country group or for Greenland, and twelve months from taking up fast bopel for Japan alone (carried on the Japanese row).

MEDICAL IS UNRECORDED BECAUSE IT IS CONDITIONAL, NOT GENERAL: a synsattest is required only where eyesight is impaired, and a helseattest only for the heavy classes or where health may affect road safety.

Residence: fast bopel in Norway documented by a bostedsattest from Skatteetaten. If the licence was obtained while the holder was registered as resident in Norway, the holder must show either fast bopel in the issuing country when it was issued, or that it was obtained during a temporary stay abroad of at least six months. The original licence is surrendered with the application.
EEA mutual recognition under Directive 2006/126/EC, which Norway applies through the EEA Agreement, is deliberately not expanded here.

SHARED BY THE EIGHT TEST-SITTING ROWS. Statens vegvesen groups these eight origins on one sub-page, https://www.vegvesen.no/forerkort/har-forerkort/utenlandsk-forerkort-i-norge/innbytte-av-forerkort-fra-land-utenfor-eu-eos/australia-canada-og-flere/ , which states that once the exchange application is granted the holder must pass both the theory test and the practical driving test ("Får du innvilget søknaden din, må du bestå teoriprøve og oppkjøring"); for BE and the truck/bus classes only the practical test in the highest class is required. Two attempts at the practical test; two years from the grant to pass. No deadline to apply for the exchange.

destinations.name: Sweden
destinations.instrument: Transportstyrelsen — Byta ut körkort från Förenade kungariket, Färöarna, Japan eller Schweiz
notes: A FOUR-ENTRY ANNEX THAT STATES ITS OWN EXHAUSTIVENESS: "Du kan byta ut ditt körkort från Förenade kungariket Storbritannien och Nordirland (Förenade kungariket), Färöarna, Schweiz eller Japan mot ett svenskt. Körkort från andra länder utanför EES kan inte bytas ut mot ett svenskt körkort."

THE TEST FIELDS ARE NULL, NOT false. Transportstyrelsen enumerates the entire procedure — application form, health declaration and eyesight certificate for AM/A1/A2/A/B/BE or a läkarintyg for the heavy classes, the original licence, and a certificate of validity from the issuing authority — and that procedure contains no examination step. It never says that no test is required. Writing false would invent a waiver out of a document that simply does not address the question; null says what is true, which is that it was not recorded.

THE ONE-YEAR CLOCK BINDS ONLY TWO OF THE FOUR, so it is carried on those two rows and not at destination level. A non-EEA licence ceases to be valid in Sweden one year from the day of folkbokföring, but the page carves out the United Kingdom and the Faroe Islands, whose licences remain usable beyond that year.

Medical evidence is required in every case. The original is surrendered: Japanese licences are returned to the Japanese embassy in Stockholm, and UK, Faroese and Swiss licences to the issuing licensing authority. Page last updated 2025-08-14. EEA mutual recognition is handled on a separate Transportstyrelsen page and is deliberately not expanded here.

SHARED BY ALL FOUR ROWS. Transportstyrelsen's page sets out the whole application (application form, health declaration and eyesight certificate for the light classes or a medical certificate for the heavy classes, the original foreign licence, and a certificate of validity from the issuing authority) and contains no driving-test step — but it does not say in terms that no test is required, so both test fields are left unrecorded rather than written as false.

entries.note: Named as "Förenade kungariket Storbritannien och Nordirland". Unlike the other three, a UK licence stays usable in Sweden beyond one year of folkbokföring, so there is no one-year exchange deadline.
Named as "Färöarna". Like the UK licence, a Faroese licence stays usable beyond one year of folkbokföring, so there is no one-year exchange deadline.
Named as "Schweiz". Subject to the one-year deadline from folkbokföring. The surrendered licence is sent back to the issuing authority.
Named as "Japan". Subject to the one-year deadline from folkbokföring. The validity certificate must be obtained from the Japanese embassy in Stockholm, and the surrendered licence is sent there.

destinations.name: Finland
destinations.instrument: Traficom — Ulkomaisen ajokortin vaihtaminen suomalaiseen ajokorttiin; list of "Sopimusvaltiot ja niihin rinnastettavat valtiot" (contracting states and states equated with them)
notes: THE WIDEST THIRD-COUNTRY ANNEX IN THE REGION, AND THE GATE IS TIMING RATHER THAN ORIGIN. Traficom publishes about 115 "sopimusvaltiot ja niihin rinnastettavat valtiot" whose licences can be exchanged. A contracting-state licence may be driven on for two years after moving permanently to Finland, and if the exchange is applied for inside that window, for a class other than BE/truck/bus, and while the entitlement is still valid, no driver's examination is required. Outside those bounds the full kuljettajantutkinto — theory AND driving test — applies: "Jos olet asunut Suomessa vakinaisesti yli 2 vuotta, ajo-oikeutesi on päättynyt tai vaihdat BE-luokan tai kuorma- ja/tai linja-auton ajokorttia, sinun pitää suorittaa kuljettajantutkinto." The 24-month deadline is therefore what buys the test waiver, and the false test flags on every row are true only inside it.

THREE LIST ENTRIES ARE NOT MAPPABLE TO ISO 3166 and are carried without a code rather than being guessed into one: "Jugoslavia" (a defunct state), "Kurdistan" (not a sovereign state, and Traficom does not say which issuing authority is meant), and "Yhdistynyt kuningaskunta ja siihen kuuluvat alusmaat", whose dependent territories are not enumerated. "Guayana" is read as Guyana, but the Finnish exonym is normally spelled "Guyana", so that mapping is inferred rather than stated.

Classes are not recorded per origin because Traficom does not map them per country. A lääkärinlausunto valid six months is required for every contracting-state exchange. The foreign licence is retained by Traficom and returned only if the holder moves out of the country; a temporary Finnish licence is issued in the interim.

Residence: "Jotta voit saada suomalaisen ajokortin, sinun tulee asua vakituisesti Suomessa". A licence first obtained while already living in Finland cannot be exchanged, though one renewed abroad while living in Finland can. Page last updated 25.6.2026. The EU/EEA list on the same page is deliberately not expanded here.

destinations.name: Poland
destinations.instrument: Ustawa z dnia 5 stycznia 2011 r. o kierujących pojazdami, art. 14 ust. 1 — consolidated text announced by Obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu z dnia 1 września 2025 r., Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1226
notes: THERE IS NO COUNTRY LIST, AND INVENTING ONE WOULD BE FABRICATING THE ANNEX. Art. 14 ust. 1 defines the classes by treaty membership: a licence "określone w konwencjach o ruchu drogowym" (defined in the road traffic conventions of art. 4 ust. 1 pkt 2 lit. a and b — Geneva, 19 September 1949, Dz. U. 1959 nr 54 poz. 321 i 322, and Vienna, 8 November 1968, Dz. U. 1988 nr 5 poz. 40 i 44) is exchanged on surrender of the foreign document; anything else additionally requires passing the theory part of the state examination and producing a certified translation. So this destination carries two rows, not a list of states.
ONLY THE THEORY PART IS IMPOSED. The statute names "części teoretycznej egzaminu państwowego" and nothing else, so the practical part is recorded as not required on the face of the provision.
Every exchange requires surrender of the foreign document to the issuing authority ("po zwrocie zagranicznego dokumentu organowi wydającemu prawo jazdy").
RESIDENCE, WINDOW AND MEDICAL ARE UNRECORDED, NOT ABSENT: art. 14 is silent on all three, and the general issuance conditions in art. 11 were not read for this row.

Art. 14 ust. 3-5 let the transport minister set different, reciprocity-based conditions for the citizens of particular states by regulation. No such regulation was located, so no bilateral rows are claimed. The EU/Switzerland/EFTA-EEA carve-out in the same sentence is the mutual-recognition rule and is deliberately not expanded as annex rows.

entries.origin_label_en: States whose national driving licence is defined in the 1949 Geneva or 1968 Vienna Road Traffic Convention
entries.note: Art. 14 ust. 1 imposes the theory-exam condition only where the foreign licence "nie jest określone w konwencjach o ruchu drogowym" (is not one defined in the road traffic conventions). A licence that is so defined is therefore exchanged on surrender of the foreign document, with no exam. Poland does not publish an enumerated country annex; the class is defined by convention membership, which is why no ISO code is given.

entries.origin_label_en: Any other state (licence not defined in the road traffic conventions)

destinations.name: Czechia
destinations.instrument: Ministerstvo dopravy — Výměna řidičského průkazu vydaného nečlenským státem EU, který svým provedením neodpovídá Úmluvám o silničním provozu (Ženeva 1949, Vídeň 1968)
notes: TWO LIMBS AND A NAMED EXCEPTION LIST, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING. Limb one: a non-EU licence whose FORM conforms to the Vienna 1968 or Geneva 1949 model is exchanged on production of an identity document and the licence alone (sibling ministry page https://www.mdcr.cz/Zivotni-situace/Ridicske-prukazy/vymena-RP-mimoEU-CZ). Limb two: a non-conforming licence is still exchangeable, but requires a přezkoušení z odborné způsobilosti k řízení motorových vozidel no older than 30 days plus a medical certificate no older than 30 days. Japan, the Republic of Korea and the United Arab Emirates are named exceptions to limb two and need neither.
THE RE-EXAMINATION IS NOT SPLIT INTO THEORY AND PRACTICAL by the ministry, so the non-conforming row leaves both fields unrecorded rather than guessing which half applies.

THE THREE-MONTH DUTY IS CARRIED HERE AND IN NEITHER CLOCK FIELD, DELIBERATELY. The ministry states that a holder with trvalý pobyt, or přechodný pobyt for more than one year, is OBLIGED to apply for the exchange within three months of the day that residence is granted (or of the day a Czech citizen returns to Czechia). That is a duty to apply. Recording either would put a consequence into the data that the source does not state.

The original is surrendered on collection of the Czech licence and is sent to the issuing state, or held by the municipal office at the holder's request. A document marked "Provisional driving licence" is expressly not exchangeable, and an expired foreign licence cannot be exchanged at all.

notes: THE ANNEX IS TWO NAMED PROCEDURES, AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEIR TITLES IS THE FINDING. Procedure 02.10 covers the U.S.A., Canada, Australia, Japan, South Africa and South Korea; procedure 02.11 covers Switzerland. Only the Swiss title states that the conversion is made "ΧΩΡΙΣ ΘΕΩΡΗΤΙΚΗ ΕΞΕΤΑΣΗ ΚΑΙ ΔΟΚΙΜΑΣΙΑ ΠΡΟΣΟΝΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΣΥΜΠΕΡΙΦΟΡΑΣ" — without theory examination and without the practical qualification-and-behaviour test.

SO SIX ROWS ARE NULL, NOT false. The 02.10 sheet sets out documents, fees and preconditions and says nothing at all about examinations. Silence in a procedure sheet is not a waiver, and a reader who is told "no test required" and then sits one at the counter has been failed by this layer. Only Switzerland is recorded as test-free, because only Switzerland's procedure title says so.

The 02.10 route is materially heavier in a second way: it additionally requires a certificate from the issuing authority confirming the licence is not withheld for any penalty, which must reach the Greek transport directorate through consular channels only. The Swiss sheet drops that requirement.
Both procedure sheets (downloadable from the same page as /getfile.php?id=6756 and id=6757) require at least two medical certificates under Annex III of π.δ. 51/2012, plus proof of fees.

Residence: συνήθης διαμονή in Greece, or six months as a student or pupil before applying; a non-Greek national must produce a residence document issued at least 185 days before the application; and the applicant must hold no other Greek, EU/EEA or third-country licence.

KYA 24058/2653/2004 also covers licences from former Soviet Union states, but no procedure sheet for that class was located on this page, so no such rows are claimed. No deadline running from the acquisition of residence is stated on either sheet, so none is recorded. EU mutual recognition is procedure 02.09 on the same page and is deliberately not expanded here.

destinations.name: Japan
destinations.instrument: 外国免許からの切替え（外免切替）— 道路交通法第97条の２第３項 (confirmation of knowledge and skill) with 道路交通法施行令第34条の４第２項 (waiver of the statutory written and practical tests); list of exempted countries/regions published by the licensing authority
notes: JAPAN EXCHANGES FROM EVERYWHERE, AND THE 29-COUNTRY LIST IS NOT THE LIST OF COUNTRIES IT EXCHANGES FROM. Two layers, and reading them as one gets the answer wrong in both directions. 道路交通法施行令第34条の4第2項 already waives the statutory 学科試験 and 技能試験 for ANY holder of a foreign Class 1 licence who stayed three months or more in the issuing country after obtaining it. What is left is an administrative 知識確認 (knowledge confirmation) and 技能確認 (skills confirmation) under 道路交通法第97条の2第3項. The published list of 29 countries and regions exempts holders from THOSE TWO CONFIRMATIONS as well. So an unlisted origin is not refused — it converts after sitting both confirmations, which is why the "any other country or territory" row records them as required rather than as no route at all.

THE US ROWS ARE SEVEN NAMED STATES PLUS INDIANA, AND JAPAN IS NOT PAINTED ONTO THE UNITED STATES FOR THEM. The instrument names アメリカ合衆国（オハイオ州、オレゴン州、コロラド州、バージニア州、ハワイ州、メリーランド州及びワシントン州に限る）for the full exemption, and Indiana separately under 技能確認を免除する国等 — skills confirmation waived, knowledge confirmation not. Licences from the other forty-three states are not exempt from either confirmation, so the United States is deliberately excluded from this agreement's beneficiaries: a painted country would tell a Texan a thing that is not true. The rows carry the parent so that a US lookup still finds Japan and sees exactly which states are named.

AUSTRALIA AND CANADA ARE LISTED COUNTRY-WIDE BY JAPAN, unlike Germany, Denmark and Switzerland, which treat both provincially, and unlike the US treatment on this very page. The two patterns are not normalised to each other here.

grants is recognition_and_exchange because Japan separately RECOGNISES the domestic licences of six jurisdictions for driving without exchange, when accompanied by a prescribed Japanese translation: 「現在、スイス連邦、ドイツ連邦共和国、フランス共和国、ベルギー王国、モナコ公国及び台湾が対象となります」 (NPA). That is recognition of the licence itself, not an International Driving Permit instrument, so it is in scope; the IDP/Geneva route is excluded from this layer.

ORIGIN-SIDE RESIDENCE CONDITION, VERBATIM: 「外国等の免許を受けた後、その国等に通算して３か月以上滞在していたことが条件となります」 — a cumulative three months or more in the issuing country AFTER the licence was obtained, evidenced by passport entry/exit stamps. The original foreign licence (not an IDP) must be produced with a Japanese translation prepared by the issuing authority, that country's consulate, JAF, ジップラス or 訪日運転者支援協会. Japan-side: an address in Japan and a 住民票 showing 特定事項.

THE ROUTE TIGHTENED ON 1 OCTOBER 2025: a 道路交通法施行規則 amendment took the knowledge confirmation from 10 questions with 7 to pass to 50 questions with 45 to pass, dropped the illustration questions, added tasks such as crossing pedestrian crossings to the skills confirmation with stricter marking, and tightened residence documentation. Source: https://www.keishicho.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/menkyo/oshirase/low.html

NO EXCHANGE DEADLINE IS RECORDED: nothing on the authority's page states one. The separate rule that a foreign or international licence may be driven on for one year from the date of landing is the driving-on-a-foreign-licence rule, keyed to landing rather than to residence and available to visitors, so it is not recorded as this destination's clock.

MEDICAL IS UNRECORDED: the authority publishes eyesight thresholds tested at the counter (0.7 both eyes / 0.3 each for ordinary and motorcycle; 0.8 / 0.5 plus depth perception for semi-medium and above) but says nothing about a certificate to be produced. Not recorded is not the same as not required. Whether the foreign licence is surrendered is likewise not stated.

The 29-item list is national and is published by each prefectural police force; this row cites the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department page (updated 17 August 2026). The NPA's own national page states the framework and the three-month condition but does not reproduce the list: https://www.npa.go.jp/policies/application/license_renewal/have_DL_issed_another_country.html
SHARED BY THE 28 FULLY EXEMPT ROWS. Listed among the 29 countries/regions exempted from both the knowledge confirmation (知識確認) and the skills confirmation (技能確認).
SHARED BY THE 7 FULLY EXEMPT ROWS. One of the seven states named inside the single listing アメリカ合衆国（…に限る）; licences from any other US state are not exempt from the two confirmations.

destinations.name: Singapore
destinations.instrument: Traffic Police, "Singapore Driving Licence" — Conversion of Foreign Driving Licence to Singapore Driving Licence (administrative criteria and document schedule)
notes: THE ONE DESTINATION HERE WITH NO ORIGIN LIST AT ALL, AND THEORY IS true FOR EVERY ORIGIN. The Traffic Police gate the applicant, not the issuing state: "The criteria for the conversion of licence are" a pass in the Basic Theory Test and a valid foreign licence. Everyone sits the BTT, wherever the licence came from, so the layer's usual question — which countries are exchangeable — has the answer "all of them, on the same terms".

PRACTICAL IS false ON A RECORDED BASIS, NOT AN INFERRED ONE. The page states the criteria exhaustively and introduces a practical test only as an addition "on top of the Basic Theory Test (BTT)" for Work Permit and S Pass holders upgrading out of Class 3C. It is a stated absence for the ordinary case, not a silence.

CLASS OUTCOME IS STRATIFIED BY IMMIGRATION STATUS, NOT BY ORIGIN: "All Work Permit & S Pass Holders will be granted a Class 3C licence upon successful conversion", limited to motor cars up to 3,000kg unladen with seven or fewer passengers. Since 15 September 2025 a Class 3C holder must also pass a road assessment before taking Class 4 lessons, and failing it revokes the 3C.

THE ORIGIN-SIDE CONDITION IS DOCUMENTARY AND IS THE REAL GATE: "Supporting documents to prove 1-year residency in country of issuance of driving licence with a physical residency of at least 6 months in the said country", whose stated purpose is "To determine intention of stay in country is not solely to obtain a driving licence". PRs, pass holders and citizens whose foreign licence was obtained after they acquired that status must additionally prove a six-month stay within a twelve-month period in the issuing country.

THE THREE-MONTH CLOCK IS A GRACE PERIOD, NOT A DEADLINE: a new Singapore citizen or permanent resident "is allowed to drive for up to three months on Singapore roads upon obtaining the new Singapore citizenship or permanent resident status and will be required to do a conversion... if he/she wishes to continue driving". A different clock applies to work-pass drivers: a Singapore licence within six months from the date of issue of the work pass.

Motorcycles are the exception where the origin authority is asked to vouch: Class 2A and Class 2 need "Proof from the foreign Licensing Authority stating a higher capacity of the motorcycle tested on", signed and endorsed by that authority. Licences not in English need an official translation by a Singapore registered translation company. Surrender of the original is not stated and is not recorded.

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: foreigners residing in Singapore for less than twelve months drive on a foreign licence plus an International Driving Permit, and ASEAN member state licence holders need no IDP at all. That is visitor recognition, not exchange, and is not made a destination fact. Fee $50, after a FormSG pre-assessment and an appointment; page last updated 30 July 2026.

entries.classes: Class 3/3A and Class 2B (age 18+); Work Permit and S Pass holders are issued Class 3C on conversion
entries.note: Singapore publishes no list of approved origin countries. The published criteria are only (i) pass the Basic Theory Test in Singapore and (ii) hold a valid foreign driving licence, so the origin state does not gate the exchange — the applicant's own residence history does. No practical test is listed for the ordinary conversion; a practical test is added only for Work Permit/S Pass holders who want Class 3 rather than the Class 3C they are given, or who want to upgrade 3C/3CA to 3/3A.

Extra origin-specific proof: "For Malaysian driving licence holder, a letter from the Road Transport Department Malaysia [Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan Malaysia (JPJ)] showing the breakdown of various class(es) of driving licence and date of issuance together with payment receipt." Malaysia also has its own downloadable checklist.

Extra origin-specific proof: "For Indian driving licence holder, an endorsement letter of validity of driving licence from India Embassy (with payment receipt)." India also has its own downloadable checklist. Note the Traffic Police treat India as a single country here — no state-level split.
Traffic Police publish a separate document checklist for China alongside Malaysia, India and "Other countries".

destinations.name: Hong Kong
destinations.instrument: Road Traffic (Driving Licences) Regulations (Cap. 374B), Schedule 4 — direct issue of a Hong Kong full driving licence without test
notes: DIRECT ISSUE IS GENUINELY TEST-FREE, AND THE DEPARTMENT SAYS SO: "Applicants meeting all the requirements for direct issue of a full driving licence would be issued with a Hong Kong full driving licence without passing through the 12-month probationary driving period."

SCOPE LIMIT WORTH CARRYING INTO ANY MAP OF THIS ROW: "The \"direct issue\" mechanism is only applicable to private car, light goods vehicle, motor cycle and motor tricycle." Heavy and public-service classes are not exchangeable by this route.

NO HONG KONG RESIDENCE IS REQUIRED, WHICH IS UNUSUAL IN THIS LAYER. The Transport Department expressly contemplates applicants living outside Hong Kong ("If you reside outside Hong Kong, you may fill in your non-Hong Kong residential address in the application form"), requiring only proof of present address plus a Hong Kong correspondence address. The residence test sits on the ORIGIN side and is disjunctive: the licence was issued during a period of residence of not less than six months in the issuing place, OR it has been held for not less than five years immediately before the application, OR the applicant holds a passport or equivalent travel document of the issuing place.

THE FOREIGN LICENCE IS NOT SURRENDERED: "Please note that the Transport Department will not keep the original identity documents and driving licences. Such documents will be returned over the counter on the spot." It must be a full licence, valid or expired for not more than three years, obtained by passing the relevant driving test in the issuing place.

SUB-NATIONAL HANDLING IS THE OPPOSITE OF JAPAN'S: Hong Kong lists the United States and Canada country-wide, with no state or province split, where Japan names seven US states and Germany, Denmark and Switzerland treat both federations provincially. The only sub-national structure in Schedule 4 is inside the "China" item (Mainland, Taiwan, Macao) and inside the composite "United Kingdom together with Alderney (with Channel Islands), Bermuda, Guernsey, Isle of Man, Jersey". The three "China" sub-items are recorded here as origins in their own right rather than as sub-units, because each has its own ISO code and its own licensing authority and a reader holding a Taiwan or Macao licence must be able to find this row by searching for it.

ORIGINS NOT IN SCHEDULE 4 ARE NOT REFUSED OUTRIGHT — they take the temporary-driving-licence route: apply for a driving test within three months of arriving to take up residence, drive on a temporary licence valid until the foreign licence expires or twelve months from arrival, whichever is first, and pass the Hong Kong test. That is a test route, not an exchange, so no rows are written for it.
MEDICAL IS false AS A RECORDED LIMIT, NOT AN INFERENCE: form TD256 completed by a registered medical practitioner within four months of application is required only for "a person aged 70 or above".

From 16 March 2026 direct-issue applications must be booked through the designated online appointment system; no walk-in tickets, no postal or drop-box submission. Since 15 September 2025 licences carrying a direct-issue entitlement are numbered with a "DI" prefix and the entitlement is marked with an asterisk. Appendix C is the Transport Department's own reproduction of Schedule 4 and carries a revision date of 23 September 2025.
SHARED BY 29 ROWS. Listed in Schedule 4 of Cap. 374B, so a full licence from this place qualifies for direct issue of a Hong Kong full driving licence without test.

destinations.name: Taiwan
destinations.instrument: 道路交通安全規則 第50條第5項及第6項 (Regulations Governing Road Traffic Safety, Article 50(5)-(6))
notes: THE EXCHANGE IS 免考 — WITHOUT EXAMINATION — BUT THE WHOLE GRANT IS CONDITIONED ON 平等互惠原則 (the principle of equality and reciprocity). Which foreign governments satisfy that is NOT in the regulation; it is an administrative list published by 公路局. That list could not be retrieved from any official host: www.thb.gov.tw returns a 200 that is an Incapsula bot-challenge shell (959 bytes, no content), www.mvdis.gov.tw times out at TCP level, tpcmv.thb.gov.tw returns a 212-byte stub, and data.gov.tw's dataset search endpoint 404s. The per-country reciprocity list is therefore treated as OPEN and recorded as one row, not invented as a country list.

A GENUINE NATIONALITY CARVE-OUT SITS IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH, AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY FROM DUBAI'S: "但持有該有效之正式駕駛執照者而具有中華民國國籍時，得免考換發同等車類之普通駕駛執照" — a holder with Republic of China nationality gets the examination-free exchange without the reciprocity qualifier attaching in the same way. Worth reading alongside the citizenship layer; it is not recorded as a nationality_gate because it widens the route for one group rather than closing it to others.

destinations.name: Türkiye
destinations.instrument: NVİ, "Sürücü Belgeleri Hizmetleri Sıkça Sorulan Sorular", item (4) — documents required to exchange a driving licence obtained abroad. The rule it implements is Karayolları Trafik Yönetmeliği m.88 (heading and text as amended RG 17/04/2015-29329 and RG 05/06/2020-31146; original RG 18/07/1997-23053 mükerrer).
notes: THE SIX MONTHS IS A GRACE PERIOD, NOT A DEADLINE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE ROW. Karayolları Trafik Yönetmeliği m.88(b): "1) Dış ülkelerden alınan sürücü belgeleri ile ülkemize giriş yapıldığı tarihten itibaren en fazla altı ay süreyle araç kullanılabilir. 2) Altı ayın sonunda ülkemizde araç kullanılabilmesi için dış ülkelerden alınan sürücü belgelerinin ülkemiz sürücü belgesi ile değiştirilmesi zorunludur." — a foreign national may drive on the foreign licence for at most six months FROM THE DATE OF ENTRY, at the end of which exchanging it for a Turkish licence is COMPULSORY. Nothing lapses; an obligation begins. Every other window in this layer runs from residence and ends in a lost right, which is why this number is carried in foreign_licence_grace_months and not in exchange_deadline_months. Turkish citizens get two years on the same article (m.88/a/1 and a/3) and must carry a notarised or consulate-certified Turkish translation once they have been in the country more than six months (m.88/a/2).

THERE IS NO COUNTRY ANNEX. m.88 opens "İlgili kanunlar ile ikili ve çok taraflı anlaşma hükümleri saklı kalmak üzere" (without prejudice to the relevant laws and to bilateral and multilateral agreements) and then applies to foreign licences generally. The three named bilaterals below are the only instruments NVİ publishes by name; they are recorded as rows because they exist, not because the general route depends on them.

SOURCE SWAP, AND WHY. The governing text is m.88 of the Karayolları Trafik Yönetmeliği, whose consolidated PDF is at https://www.mevzuat.gov.tr/MevzuatMetin/yonetmelik/7.5.8182.pdf and which was read in full — but mevzuat.gov.tr serves an INCOMPLETE certificate chain (leaf CN=*.tccb.gov.tr issued by GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1, no intermediate presented), so the repo's fetch fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE and the quote gate scores it HTTP 0. curl succeeds because it chases the AIA; the gate does not. The row is therefore anchored on NVİ, which the gate fetches cleanly and which is the authority m.88 itself points to for the documents.

TESTS ARE UNRECORDED ON EVERY ROW, DELIBERATELY. Neither m.88 nor the NVİ document list mentions a theory or practical test, and NVİ lists the driving-school certificate ("motorlu taşıt sürücüsü sertifikası") as a requirement for ORIGINAL issue and not in the exchange list — but silence in a document checklist is not a waiver, so both fields stay null and no row claims a test-free exchange.

MEDICAL IS true ON THE FACE OF THE SOURCE: NVİ's exchange list is the original foreign licence plus a colour photocopy, a notarised or consulate-certified Turkish translation, an identity document, a "Sürücü sağlık raporu", the fee, one biometric photograph taken within six months, blood group, an education certificate with a notarised translation if obtained abroad, and a criminal record certificate. The health report is taken from a health institution authorised by the Ministry of Health, against the Sürücü Adayları ve Sürücülerde Aranacak Sağlık Şartları ile Muayenelerine Dair Yönetmelik (RG 26/09/2006-26301).

SURRENDER IS NOT STATED for the exchange case: NVİ requires the ORIGINAL foreign licence plus a colour photocopy, which implies deposit but does not say so, and m.88 is silent. Not recorded as a finding.

RESIDENCE: m.88 keys the clock to date of entry rather than to residence. m.92 separately provides that foreign nationals residing on a residence permit ("ikamet tezkeresi ile ikamet eden yabancı uyruklular"), stateless persons, diplomats and foreign technical and administrative staff have their foreign licences exchanged under the m.88 rules, but may not drive Turkish-registered vehicles for gain or commercially.

Türkiye also appears as an ORIGIN on the RTA Dubai row in this corpus, where the licence is accepted from holders of any nationality but requires a Driving Licence Data Certificate from the Turkish consulate or embassy, certified by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

destinations.name: Argentina
destinations.instrument: Bilateral agreements on reciprocal recognition and exchange of driving licences listed by the ANSV ('Consulta sobre los Acuerdos Internacionales de Licencias de Conducir'); the domestic licence framework is Ley 24.449 / Licencia Nacional de Conducir
notes: FIVE NAMED INSTRUMENTS AND NOTHING ELSE. The ANSV's agreements index lists exactly five: Bolivia, Chile, Colombia (by equivalence rather than exchange), Spain and Italy. No general non-treaty exchange route for other nationalities was found on argentina.gob.ar — that is an absence of evidence, not evidence that none exists, and no open row is written on the strength of it.

THE TEST FIELDS DIFFER BY INSTRUMENT, WHICH IS WHY THEY ARE PER ROW. Chile and Colombia state the exemption in terms ("estando exento de los realizar los exámenes teóricos ni prácticos"; "sin estar obligados a realizar los exámenes teóricos y prácticos"), while the Bolivian, Spanish and Italian pages carry no procedural detail at all and are therefore unrecorded on both fields.

THE TWELVE-MONTH DEADLINE IS A CLAIM DEADLINE: "El trámite debe realizarse dentro de los 365 días desde la adquisición de la condición de residente en el territorio argentino" (Colombia page), and the Chile page requires the application "dentro del primer año de residencia en la Argentina". The foreign licence must have been valid and issued BEFORE residence was obtained.

PROCESS: e-mail the ANSV with scans; the ANSV verifies validity with the issuing authority and issues a "Certificado para otorgamiento de Licencia Nacional de Conducir por Canje" (valid 90 days, 60 in the Colombian equivalence route); the applicant then attends the Centro Emisor de Licencias for their domicile, pays the CENAT, sits the examen psicofísico and collects the Argentine licence.

The Licencia Nacional de Conducir is issued by municipal and provincial Centros Emisores, but the exchange authorisation certificate is issued centrally by the ANSV, so this destination is national rather than sub-national. Medical is true: the Chile, Bolivia and Colombia pages each require the examen psicofísico.

entries.note: Agreement signed 26 January 2021. ANSV page https://www.argentina.gob.ar/servicio/acuerdo-entre-la-republica-argentina-y-la-republica-de-chile-sobre-reconocimiento-reciproco states the applicant must be a Chilean 'dentro del primer año de residencia en la Argentina' holding a valid Chilean licence issued before residence, and at the Centro Emisor de Licencias: 'Realizá el examen psicofísico, estando exento de los realizar los exámenes teóricos ni prácticos.' A practical competence test IS required for the Argentine equivalents of classes B2, E2, G1, G2 and G3; professional licences used commercially are excluded from the recognition limb. The Chilean licence is surrendered.

Agreement signed 4 July 2023 at the LXII Mercosur Common Market Council meeting. ANSV page https://www.argentina.gob.ar/servicio/acuerdo-entre-la-republica-de-argentina-y-el-estado-plurinacional-de-bolivia-sobre requires the Bolivian licence to be valid and issued before residence was obtained, and lists 'Realizá el examen psicofísico' at the Centro Emisor de Licencias. That page does not state whether theory or practical examinations apply, so both are left unrecorded. The Bolivian licence is surrendered.

Titulares de Licencia de Conducir españolas vigentes con residencia en la Argentina') but the published page carries no procedural detail beyond that, so exam requirements are unrecorded.
