destinations.name: Brazil
destinations.instrument: Resolução CONTRAN nº 933, de 28 de março de 2022 (DOU 01/04/2022, Seção 1, p. 122), issued under art. 142 of the Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (Lei nº 9.503/1997)
notes: NO COUNTRY LIST, AND THE INSTRUMENT SAYS WHY. Art. 2 §2: "O órgão máximo executivo de trânsito da União informará aos demais órgãos ou entidades do Sistema Nacional de Trânsito (SNT) a que países se aplica o disposto neste artigo" — the list of states whose licences Brazil recognises lives with SENATRAN and was not located, so this destination is modelled as the two classes the Resolution itself creates: a licence Brazil recognises, and a licence it does not. Inventing an origin list would be fabricating the annex.

THE CONTRAST INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT IS WHAT SETS THE PRACTICAL FLAG. Art. 3 (the non-recognised case) requires the Exame de Aptidão Física e Mental, the Avaliação Psicológica AND the Exame de Direção Veicular; art. 2 §4 (the recognised case) requires the first two and omits the third. So practical is true on one row and false on the other, on the strength of a deliberate difference in the same text. Neither article mentions a written examination, so theory is unrecorded on both.

THE 180 DAYS IS A GRACE PERIOD: "O condutor estrangeiro, após o prazo de 180 (cento e oitenta) dias de estada regular no Brasil, pretendendo continuar a dirigir veículo automotor no âmbito territorial brasileiro, deverá submeter-se aos Exames..." — the foreign licence carries the holder for 180 days of regular stay, after which a CNH is needed to keep driving. It is carried on the recognised-licence row, which is the one art. 2 §4 governs.

LEGAL CHAIN: CTB (Lei 9.503/1997) art. 142 subordinates recognition of a foreign licence to international conventions and agreements and to CONTRAN's rules; Resolução CONTRAN 933/2022 revoked Resoluções 360/2010 and 671/2017, and a DOU full-text search for later instruments citing it returned no amending act. Resolução CONTRAN 789/2020 independently confirms the route: art. 5º IV lists "substituição do documento de habilitação obtido em país estrangeiro" among the cases requiring the Exame de Aptidão Física e Mental.

The Planalto consolidated text of the CTB is served in ISO-8859-1 and renders as mojibake through the extraction pipeline, which is why the DOU publication is the cited source. Exchange is done at the state or Federal District transit authority (DETRAN); there is no fixed application deadline.

entries.origin_label_en: Any foreign licence-issuing country whose licence is NOT recognised by Brazil
entries.note: Art. 3 of Resolução CONTRAN 933/2022 (the quoted text). Exchange ('troca da sua habilitação de origem pela equivalente nacional') is done at the state/Federal District transit authority (DETRAN) and requires passing the Exame de Aptidão Física e Mental, the Avaliação Psicológica and the Exame de Direção Veicular (practical). The article enumerates no written/theory examination, but it does not state that one is waived, so theory_test_required is left unrecorded.

entries.origin_label_en: Any foreign licence-issuing country whose licence IS recognised by Brazil (international convention, bilateral agreement, or the principle of reciprocity)
entries.note: Art. 2 §4 of the same Resolution, verbatim: 'O condutor estrangeiro, após o prazo de 180 (cento e oitenta) dias de estada regular no Brasil, pretendendo continuar a dirigir veículo automotor no âmbito territorial brasileiro, deverá submeter-se aos Exames de Aptidão Física e Mental e Avaliação Psicológica, nos termos do art. 147 do Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB), respeitada a sua categoria, com vistas à obtenção da Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH).' practical_test_required is recorded false because art. 3 expressly adds 'e de Direção Veicular' for the non-recognised case while art. 2 §4 omits it — a deliberate contrast inside the same instrument. No theory examination is mentioned in either article, so theory_test_required is left unrecorded. The list of countries to which art. 2 applies is not in the Resolution: art. 2 §2 says 'O órgão máximo executivo de trânsito da União informará aos demais órgãos ou entidades do Sistema Nacional de Trânsito (SNT) a que países se aplica o disposto neste artigo' — that SENATRAN country list was not located, so no per-country ISO codes are recorded.

destinations.name: Chile
destinations.instrument: DFL Nº 1 de 2007 (Ministerio de Transportes y Telecomunicaciones), Fija texto refundido, coordinado y sistematizado de la Ley de Tránsito Nº 18.290 — art. 15 (originally art. 14 bis of Ley 18.290)
notes: AN OPEN ROUTE, NOT A RECIPROCITY LIST: "A los residentes en Chile que estén en posesión de licencias extranjeras, se les podrá otorgar la que soliciten, siempre que acrediten, en su caso, la antigüedad requerida en la Clase correspondiente y cumplan con los demás requisitos aplicables a la licencia de conducir de que se trate." Any foreign licence held by a Chilean resident, with no country list and no treaty condition.

BOTH TEST FIELDS ARE null, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE ANSWER SITS IN A DIFFERENT ARTICLE. The concession art. 15 grants is that the foreign licence can prove the "antigüedad" normally required in the lower class; the "demás requisitos aplicables" it points to include art. 13's requirement to "Acreditar conocimientos teóricos y prácticos de conducción". Reading a test requirement across articles is an inference about exchange applicants, not a statement about them, so neither field is recorded.

SOURCE NOTE: the bcn.cl navegar page is a JavaScript single-page app that yields no extractable text, so the official XML rendering of the same consolidated norm (obtxml, idNorma=1007469) is cited. In that official text the marginal amendment citations are physically interleaved with the operative sentence, which is why the verified quote contains them.

The Chilean side of the 26 January 2021 Chile–Argentina agreement is administered by the Subsecretaría de Transportes, whose host refused all connections from this environment (ECONNREFUSED), so nothing from it is recorded here; the Argentine side of that same agreement IS carried, on the Argentina row.

Diplomatic and consular agents accredited in Chile have a stronger entitlement under the same article ("bastando que para ello exhiban una licencia vigente"), which is out of scope for a residence data layer. Art. 5 lets tourists drive on their home licence for the duration of their tourist authorisation — a visitor rule, deliberately excluded. Licences are issued by the Departamento de Tránsito of the applicant's comuna.

entries.note: The statute is open to all residents holding any foreign licence, with no country list and no treaty condition. It does not itself waive or impose the examinations: it says the applicant must 'cumplan con los demás requisitos aplicables', which under art. 13 of the same law include 'Acreditar conocimientos teóricos y prácticos de conducción, así como de las disposiciones legales y reglamentarias que rigen al tránsito público'. Because that is an inference across articles rather than an explicit statement about exchange applicants, theory_test_required and practical_test_required are left unrecorded. The concession the article does grant is that the foreign licence can be used to prove the seniority ('antigüedad') normally required in the lower class.

destinations.name: Costa Rica
destinations.instrument: Ley N.º 9078, Ley de Tránsito por Vías Públicas Terrestres y Seguridad Vial, artículo 91 ("Homologación de las licencias expedidas en el extranjero"), inciso b), publicada en La Gaceta, Alcance N.º 165 de 26 de octubre de 2012
notes: AN OPEN ROUTE ON THE FACE OF THE STATUTE: art. 91(b) is available to any holder of a valid foreign licence with uninterrupted stay in the country of more than three months and lawful residence under immigration law. There is no country list and no reciprocity condition, so this destination carries one row rather than an invented annex.

THE PRACTICAL TEST IS EXPRESSLY WAIVED AND THE THEORY POSITION IS NOT STATED. Art. 91(b)(ii) requires compliance with everything the law demands for the class being homologated "excepto la obligación de atender el curso básico de educación vial y de realizar la prueba práctica". No standalone theory examination appears in art. 84's list of requirements — the theory content sits inside the curso básico, which is also waived — but the law does not address a theory test for homologación in terms, so that field is left unrecorded rather than written as waived.

MEDICAL IS true THROUGH THE SAME ROUTE THE TEST WAIVER RUNS ON: art. 91(b)(ii) requires compliance with every other requirement of the law, and art. 84(c) requires "un dictamen médico general realizado por un profesional en ciencias médicas, autorizado por el Colegio de Médicos y Cirujanos".

Art. 91(a) — the three-month tourist and transit allowance — is a visitor-driving rule and is deliberately not recorded as an exchange. For professional classes B-4 and C, art. 91(c) allows prior experience on the equivalent foreign licence to be credited, but the applicant must take the specific course for that vehicle type.

SOURCE NOTE: the Imprenta Nacional gazette PDF of the law as enacted is cited because the consolidated text could not be reached — www.pgrweb.go.cr (SCIJ) fails TLS verification in the repo's fetch pipeline, and www.educacionvial.go.cr and www.csv.go.cr both return Cloudflare 403. The post-2012 consolidated text of art. 91 could not therefore be cross-checked for later amendments.

entries.classes: The Costa Rican class/type equivalent to the foreign licence held. For professional classes B-4 and C, article 91(c) additionally allows prior experience on the equivalent foreign licence to be credited, but the applicant must take the specific course for that vehicle type.
entries.note: The practical driving test is expressly waived by article 91(b)(ii). No standalone theory examination appears in article 84's list of requirements — the theory content sits inside the "curso básico de educación vial", which article 91(b)(ii) also waives — but the law does not state in terms whether a theory test applies to homologación, so this is left unrecorded rather than written as waived.

destinations.name: Panama
destinations.instrument: Trámite de "Homologación de licencia" (ATTT/SERTRACEN); requirements cite Ley 146 de 15 de abril de 2020 and article 113 acápite b.1 of the reglamento de tránsito
notes: TWO ROUTES, AND THE MAIN ONE HAS NO RECIPROCITY LIST — CONTRARY TO THE WORKING ASSUMPTION THIS ROW WAS OPENED WITH. (1) A universal "homologación" open to holders of any foreign national driving licence, one time only, and only "al momento en que se solicite por primera vez una licencia de conducir panameña". (2) A bilateral "canje" under the Spain–Panama convenio with a published category equivalence table. Both are operated by SERTRACEN on behalf of the ATTT.

THE GATE ON THE UNIVERSAL ROUTE IS DOCUMENTARY, NOT NATIONAL: the physical foreign licence plus a certification and cotejo issued by the issuing authority or that country's consulate or embassy in Panama, authenticated by apostille, consular refrendo or diplomatic mission.

EVERY TEST AND MEDICAL FIELD IS null BECAUSE THE REQUIREMENTS ARE CONDITIONAL RATHER THAN GENERAL: a visual and auditory validation is done at the branch; a blood type/RH lab result only if the foreign licence does not show it; a general medical certificate only from age 70; a practical skills test only from age 85 and for category-D-equivalent categories. Recording false would flatten a set of age- and class-dependent conditions into a blanket waiver.

THE SPANISH ROUTE PUBLISHES ITS OWN EQUIVALENCE TABLE and its own conditions: one-time canje, the Spanish licence surrendered, certification and cotejo from the Spanish embassy or consulate in Panama, and applicants moving up to the categories equivalent to Spanish C1 and C must sit the theoretical and practical test for those vehicles.

SOURCE NOTE: transito.gob.pa, the ATTT's own site, did not respond at all during this research (connection timeout on both http and https), so SERTRACEN — the ATTT's licensing concessionaire, whose pages state ATTT procedures and cite the reglamento de tránsito — is the source used. Foreigners on temporary residence get a licence valid until the carné de migración expires or up to four years.

entries.classes: Panamanian equivalents of categories A, B, C and D. Public-transport categories are excluded (article 113 acápite b.1); foreigners on a limited migratory status may only obtain A, B and C. International driving permits and minors' permits are not homologated.
entries.note: No country list or reciprocity condition is published for the homologación route: the gate is documentary — the physical foreign licence plus a certification and cotejo issued by the issuing authority or by that country's consulate/embassy in Panama, authenticated by apostille, consular refrendo or diplomatic mission. A visual and auditory validation is done at the branch; a blood type/RH lab result is required only if the foreign licence does not show it; a general medical certificate is required only from age 70; a practical skills test is required only from age 85 and for category-D-equivalent categories. Because these are conditional, theory/practical/medical are left unrecorded rather than asserted either way.

entries.classes: Published equivalence table: Spanish A2→Panamanian B, B→C, C1→D, C→F, C+E→G, D1→E2 (not available to foreigners), D→E3 and F (foreigners only F). Panamanian categories A, E1, H and I are not exchangeable.
entries.note: Separate bilateral route documented at https://www.sertracen.com.pa/canje-de-licencia-de-conducir-espanola/ under the "Convenio entre el Reino de España y República de Panamá": one-time canje, the Spanish licence must be surrendered, and the certification/cotejo must come from the Spanish embassy or consulate in Panama. That page states that applicants moving up to the categories equivalent to Spanish C1 (Panamanian D) and C (Panamanian F) must sit the theoretical and practical test for those vehicles; for the ordinary car categories it states practical validation is required only for types D, E2, E3, F and G. Quote not taken from that URL because this dataset carries one row per destination; the quote above is from the homologación page.

destinations.name: Uruguay
destinations.instrument: gub.uy trámite 'Canje de permiso de conducir extranjero de países con convenio - Canelones' (treaty route) and 'Revalida de permiso de conducir extranjero - Canelones' (general route)
notes: ONE TREATY IN FORCE AND ONE THAT LAPSED, BOTH ON THE SAME PAGE: "Países con convenio: España. Actualmente en vigencia. Italia. Venció en el año 2019." Italy is deliberately NOT recorded as an exchange row — the page states the treaty expired and directs those holders to the revalida route instead.

THE SECOND ROW IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT WEARING THE SAME PAGE: the "revalida" is a unilateral domestic conversion open to any valid foreign permit regardless of treaty, and it is capped — "En el trámite de revalida se le otorgará permiso de conducir en categorías A, G1 o G2 según corresponda a la conversión sobre el permiso que posee en el extranjero. No se otorga mediante este trámites categorías superiores a las indicadas."

BOTH ROWS ARE null ON BOTH TEST FIELDS, AND THE PAGES ARE THE REASON. The trámite is described as proceeding "previa aprobación de los exámenes correspondientes" without saying which, and the requirement lists name only the Certificado de Aptitud Psicofísica. The Intendencia de Maldonado publishes the Spanish route in more detail: categories A, B, C, D, E, F, H, G1, G2 and G3 admitted, a practical examination compulsory only from age 75 (amateur) or 69 (professional).

Driving permits are issued by the 19 departmental Intendencias under the national Permiso Único Nacional de Conducir framework, so there is no single national counter; gub.uy is the official national portal that publishes each Intendencia's trámite, and the Canelones pages were used because they state both routes. The Spanish permit is surrendered and returned to the Dirección General de Tráfico de España; the revalida requires a driver-record certificate legalised or apostilled by the issuing authority, with notarial certification expressly not accepted.

No national gazette instrument for the Uruguay–Spain agreement was located: impo.com.uy's law base has no full-text search reachable by URL, and parlamento.gub.uy returned HTTP 403 to this environment.

entries.note: The only treaty exchange currently in force. Same page, verbatim: 'Países con convenio: España. Actualmente en vigencia. Italia. Venció en el año 2019.' The Spanish permit is surrendered and returned to the Dirección General de Tráfico de España. Requirements listed are identity document, surrender of the permit, no unpaid fines, no active disqualification, and an 'Examen psicofísico de aptitud para conducir'. The page's opening sentence refers to 'previa aprobación de los exámenes correspondientes' without saying which, and the requirement list names only the psychophysical examination, so theory and practical are left unrecorded. The Intendencia de Maldonado publishes the same route in more detail (https://www.gub.uy/tramites/licencia-conducir-canje-espana-maldonado): categories A, B, C, D, E, F, H, G1, G2 and G3 are admitted, a Certificado de Aptitud Psicofísica is required, a judicial-record certificate is required for professional categories, and a practical examination is compulsory only from age 75 (amateur categories) or age 69 (professional categories).

entries.classes: Converted only into categories A, G1 or G2
entries.note: Separate 'revalida' route, open to any valid foreign permit regardless of treaty: https://www.gub.uy/tramites/revalida-permiso-conducir-extranjero-canelones — 'Trámite mediante el cual se gestiona la conversión de permisos de conducir extranjeros que se encuentren en vigencia, con la previa aprobación de los exámenes necesarios.' Requirements: Uruguayan cédula or passport; a driver-record certificate issued and legalised/apostilled by the authority that issued the permit (notarial certification is expressly not accepted); sworn translation of any non-Spanish document; surrender of any Uruguayan permit held; no unpaid fines; no active disqualification; Certificado de Aptitud Psicofísica. Scope limit, verbatim: 'En el trámite de revalida se le otorgará permiso de conducir en categorías A, G1 o G2 según corresponda a la conversión sobre el permiso que posee en el extranjero. No se otorga mediante este trámites categorías superiores a las indicadas.' The page says examinations are required but does not identify them, so theory and practical are left unrecorded.

agreements.name: EU/EEA — mutual recognition of driving licences
agreements.instrument: Directive 2006/126/EC art. 2(1); extended to the EEA EFTA states by EEA Joint Committee Decision No 29/2008 (Annex XIII point 24f)
agreements.basis: Art. 2(1): "Driving licences issued by Member States shall be mutually recognised." Quote-checked 2026-08-09 against the EUR-Lex text. Scope is the EU-27 plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway = 30. Switzerland is NOT covered: it is not a party to the EEA Agreement (art. 126(1) lists only the three EFTA states, and art. 128 still records Switzerland as a state that may apply), so Swiss licences travel on national third-country law — Germany places Switzerland in Anlage 11 to FeV s.31, the list of states OUTSIDE the EEA. The UK is likewise a third country since the transition ended on 31 December 2020.
agreements.exchange_article: Art. 11(1): a holder who has taken up normal residence in another Member State "may request that his driving licence be exchanged for an equivalent licence". Exchange is a right to REQUEST, not automatic, and is a separate article from the art. 2(1) recognition right.
agreements.residence_condition: Art. 12: normal residence means where a person usually lives "at least 185 days in each calendar year". It gates issuance (art. 7(1)(e)) and triggers the exchange right, and art. 7(5)(a) bars holding more than one licence.
agreements.third_country_carve_out: Art. 11(6) is the provision that forecloses licence laundering. Where a Member State exchanges a THIRD-COUNTRY licence for a Community model, the exchange "shall be recorded on the Community model driving licence", the original "has been surrendered", and if the holder then moves to another Member State "the latter need not apply the principle of mutual recognition set out in Article 2". So a non-EEA licence swapped in one member state does not reliably become EEA-wide.
agreements.superseded_note: Directive (EU) 2025/2205 repeals 2006/126/EC with effect from 26 November 2029; mutual recognition moves to its art. 3(6) and the residence test becomes a rolling "185 days of the previous 365 days" (art. 20(1)) rather than a calendar-year test.
agreements.exclusivity: Art. 7(5)(a): "No person may hold more than one driving licence". Art. 7(5)(b): a Member State "shall refuse to issue a licence where it establishes that the applicant already holds a driving licence", and art. 7(5)(c)-(d) require verification with other Member States via the EU driving licence network. Exclusivity is enforced and cross-checked, not merely asserted.

agreements.name: Nordic agreement on mutual recognition and exchange of driving licences (1985)
agreements.instrument: Overenskomst 1985 om gjensidig godkjennelse av førerkort og registrering av kjøretøyer, arts. 1 and 3 (Norwegian implementation FOR-1986-07-01-3055)
agreements.basis: The only true multilateral EXCHANGE instrument found outside the EU. Art. 1 gives recognition: "Et førerkort som er utstedt i det ene landet er gyldig i de øvrige land i samsvar med sitt innhold." Art. 3 gives exchange without re-testing: a holder "kan søke om å få byttet sitt førerkort med et tilsvarende førerkort i det land hvor han er innmeldt i folkeregisteret uten å avlegge ny førerprøve" — may apply to exchange for a corresponding licence in the country where they are registered, without taking a new driving test. Both quote-checked against Lovdata 2026-08-09.
agreements.exchange_article: Art. 3, and note the trigger: exchange is available in the country where the holder is REGISTERED IN THE POPULATION REGISTER (innmeldt i folkeregisteret), which is a residence test in the same family as the EU normal-residence rule.
agreements.membership_note: ICELAND IS NOT A PARTY. The text names Danmark, Finland, Norge and Sverige and does not mention Island at all — verified by absence, not assumed. This matters because Iceland IS in the Nordic Passport Union and the Nordic common labour market, so a Nordic member list assembled for movement purposes is wrong here. Iceland is instead covered via the EEA route into Directive 2006/126/EC.

agreements.name: Germany — Anlage 11 FeV (zu § 31)
agreements.instrument: Anlage 11 FeV (zu § 31)
agreements.basis: Anlage 11 FeV is a domestic annex to a German regulation, not an agreement: Germany lists which licences it will accept and can amend the annex alone.

agreements.name: United Kingdom (Great Britain) — Driving Licences (Exchangeable Licences) Orders
agreements.instrument: Driving Licences (Exchangeable Licences) Orders — SI 1999/1641 (as amended) and SI 2021/537
agreements.basis: The Driving Licences (Exchangeable Licences) Orders are domestic statutory instruments designating which licences GB will exchange.

agreements.name: Netherlands — RDW
agreements.instrument: Regeling omwisseling niet-Nederlandse rijbewijzen art. 1 (country list), made under Reglement rijbewijzen art. 46(5)
agreements.basis: CORRECTION: our record described this as "countries outside EU/EFTA WITH AGREEMENT". There is no negotiated arrangement anywhere in the chain. Art. 1 reads "Voor omwisseling tegen een Nederlands rijbewijs komen in aanmerking de door de hierna [genoemde landen]" — a list the Netherlands designates. The word Overeenkomst in the Reglement refers to the EEA Agreement, never to a bilateral deal with an issuing state. Art. 2 is more unilateral still: RDW may exchange any foreign licence "om redenen, aan het algemeen belang ontleend" (for reasons of general interest), a discretionary domestic power with no counterparty.

agreements.name: Ireland — NDLS / RSA
agreements.instrument: Negotiated bilateral agreement/MoU, given domestic effect by Road Traffic Act 1961 s. 23A and the Road Traffic (Recognition of Foreign Driving Licences) Order 2007 (S.I. 527/2007), Schedule
agreements.basis: Genuinely two-layered, and forcing one label would lose the point. SUBSTANTIVELY bilateral: Ireland negotiates a reciprocal MoU, and the Department states agreements "may be made only when the authorities in each jurisdiction have studied and compared the licensing regimes". FORMALLY unilateral: s. 23A gives the Minister an order-making power and S.I. 527/2007 simply declares licences from "a state mentioned in the Schedule" recognised for exchange, so Ireland could delist without the counterparty. Recorded as bilateral_agreement because that is what creates the entry; the unilateral instrument is the delivery mechanism, not the deal.

agreements.name: France — Liste de réciprocité hors UE/EEE
agreements.instrument: Liste de réciprocité hors UE/EEE — Ministère de l’Intérieur / Sécurité routière (mise à jour 1er mai 2026)
agreements.basis: Published as a "liste de reciprocite": inclusion rests on a reciprocal arrangement with the issuing state.

agreements.name: Spain — DGT
agreements.instrument: DGT — Países con convenio de canjes (actualizado 26/06/2026)
agreements.basis: DGT publishes the list as "Paises con convenio de canjes" — countries with an exchange CONVENIO. The convenios are negotiated bilateral agreements, mostly with Latin America.

agreements.name: Austria — oesterreich.gv.at
agreements.instrument: FSG-DV § 9 Abs. 1 (state list), made under FSG § 23 Abs. 3 Z 5
agreements.basis: FSG-DV § 9: the driving entitlement of the listed non-EEA states "gilt gemäß Paragraph 23, Absatz 3, Ziffer 5, FSG als unter den gleichen Voraussetzungen erteilt wie in Österreich" — deemed granted under the same conditions as in Austria. A one-way equivalence test with no counterparty. NOTE: the multilateral conventions cited in FSG § 23(1) and (5) (Paris 1930, Geneva 1955, Vienna 1982) govern DRIVING ON a foreign licence as a visitor, not exchange, and must not pull this toward multilateral_instrument.

agreements.name: New Zealand — Waka Kotahi NZTA
agreements.instrument: Waka Kotahi NZTA — Converting to a New Zealand driver licence (exempt countries)
agreements.basis: No trans-Tasman or bilateral licence instrument exists. The Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition Arrangement does NOT cover driver licensing — its 41 titles cover occupations, patents, banking and accounting, and the Federal Register of Legislation returns no Commonwealth driver-licence instrument at all. Each side recognises the other unilaterally, and the asymmetry is itself the proof: Queensland gives New Zealand a bespoke statutory category (Transport Operations (Road Use Management-Driver Licensing) Regulation 2021), Western Australia lists it among 35 in a DEPARTMENTAL list, and Victoria has no list in legislation at all. Three architectures for one relationship is not an agreement. NOTE: the NZTA exempt-country list could not be re-verified — legislation.govt.nz is behind an AWS WAF and the NZTA page returns 403 to automated fetches, so the underlying entries remain as originally seeded.

agreements.name: Australia — Austroads
agreements.instrument: Austroads — Recognised overseas jurisdictions for Australian driver licences
agreements.basis: No trans-Tasman or bilateral licence instrument exists. The Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition Arrangement does NOT cover driver licensing — its 41 titles cover occupations, patents, banking and accounting, and the Federal Register of Legislation returns no Commonwealth driver-licence instrument at all. Each side recognises the other unilaterally, and the asymmetry is itself the proof: Queensland gives New Zealand a bespoke statutory category (Transport Operations (Road Use Management-Driver Licensing) Regulation 2021), Western Australia lists it among 35 in a DEPARTMENTAL list, and Victoria has no list in legislation at all. Three architectures for one relationship is not an agreement. Australian licensing is state-level, so "Australia" here is an aggregate of state instruments rather than one federal list.

agreements.name: Denmark — Danish Road Traffic Authority
agreements.instrument: BEK nr 203 af 04/03/2016 om ombytning af udenlandsk kørekort til dansk kørekort uden kontrollerende køreprøve, §§ 1-3
agreements.basis: The sharpest case for why kind matters. It LOOKS bilateral because the counterparty initiates: "Deltagelse i ordningen sker på baggrund af en ansøgning fra det pågældende land/delstat" — participation happens on the basis of an application FROM the country concerned. But no agreement is concluded; Færdselsstyrelsen decides alone and § 3 stk. 2 makes the decision unappealable to any other administrative authority. Initiation by a counterparty is not reciprocity. CORRECTION: our instrument string said "Group 1 / Group 2", conflating two different things — in BEK 550/2026 those are VEHICLE-category groups for medical fitness, while the country grouping is the separate § 1 and § 2 tracks of BEK 203/2016, labelled gruppe 1-/gruppe 2-lande on the agency site only.

agreements.name: Portugal — IMT / gov.pt
agreements.instrument: Decreto-Lei n.º 46/2022 de 12 de julho, amending Código da Estrada arts. 125.º and 128.º
agreements.basis: CORRECTION: our record described this as "OECD/CPLP and bilaterals", which implies a CPLP instrument. There is none — the CPLP Secretariat's own register of 39 intra-CPLP agreements contains nothing on driving licences or road traffic. Portugal's treatment is unilateral domestic law. DL 46/2022 in fact DISPENSES with exchange for these states: "promove-se a dispensa das trocas de cartas de condução, habilitando-se a condução no território nacional com títulos emitidos naqueles Estados, através do reconhecimento" — recognition replaces the swap. Where a holder does choose to exchange, art. 128.º(2)(a) waives the driving test. Recognition under art. 125.º(1)(c) is itself conditional on the issuing state being party to Geneva 1949 or Vienna 1968, or holding a bilateral with Portugal — and IMT names only Angola, Cabo Verde, Mozambique and São Tomé e Príncipe as having such a bilateral.

agreements.name: Switzerland — bilateral licence agreements (SR 0.741.531.*)
agreements.instrument: Fifteen instruments in the Fedlex classified compilation, SR 0.741.531.917.2 through SR 0.741.531.951.8
agreements.basis: Fifteen separate instruments read one by one against their own Fedlex texts, not one list: exchanges of notes (Belgium 1971, Hungary 1971, Greece 1980, Spain 1998), departmental arrangements (Luxembourg 1973 with the Federal Department of Justice and Police; Ontario, Saskatchewan, Prince Edward Island, Alberta and Newfoundland with DETEC; Manitoba with OFROU/ASTRA) and full accords (Louisiana 2001, Quebec 2004, Liechtenstein 2015, Italy 2021). Two things fall out of reading them. First, the Belgian, Greek, Hungarian and Luxembourg notes were reported as recognition-only and are not: each also grants exchange without an examination, in Luxembourg under an article headed «Renonciation à l'examen de conduire». Second, and the reason this agreement paints seven countries out of fifteen partners: EIGHT PARTNERS ARE SUB-NATIONAL. Seven Canadian provinces and the US state of Louisiana concluded these instruments themselves — Louisiana under the state-law power in La. R.S. 32:404(F), the provinces through their own ministers and insurers — and nowhere in the SR 0.741.531 series is there a Swiss treaty with Canada or with the United States. Those rows carry no country ISO and no parent ISO, and are not beneficiaries; painting Canada or the USA, even partially, would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist on the strength of eight sub-units. They are readable in the table instead, which is where a partner that is not a country belongs. The six Canadian letter-exchanges quote the Switzerland-to-province leg and are expressly conditional on Swiss reciprocity, so the instrument is bilateral while the inbound examination treatment stays unrecorded. grants is recorded at the FLOOR, not the maximum: all fifteen grant exchange and fourteen also grant recognition, Italy's 2021 accord recognising licences only «aux fins de l'échange». A field that sits on the agreement cannot carry a family that varies, so it carries the value true of every member and the upgrades are named on the rows.

agreements.name: South Korea — bilateral licence treaties (MOFA register)
agreements.instrument: Nineteen 고시-numbered instruments in the MOFA treaty register, 운전면허 상호인정 category
agreements.basis: The KIND is what this source establishes, and it establishes it well: nineteen instruments published in the MOFA treaty register under their own 고시 numbers, simplified-form international agreements concluded without National Assembly consent. 도로교통법 s.84(2)'s final proviso speaks of an 약정 (arrangement) rather than a 조약 (treaty), but that is drafting breadth, not a downgrade, so bilateral_agreement is the right type. GRANTS IS READ FROM THE TITLE, NOT THE OPERATIVE TEXT. All nineteen rows cite the same register listing, which proves each instrument exists and what it is called and carries none of its articles; fifteen titles say 상호 인정 및 교환 (mutual recognition and exchange), Colombia's says 인정 또는 교환 (recognition OR exchange), and Belgium's, Italy's and Chile's say recognition alone. grants is therefore recorded at the FLOOR shared by all nineteen — recognition — rather than the widest value, which would overstate three rows; the floor is also the substantively right reading, since the exchange itself is issuance of a Korean licence under s.84(1)3 and s.84(3), a domestic act the treaty does not perform. Class matching is asserted for three rows only — Belgium, Italy and Poland — because KoRoad, the issuing authority, names exactly five countries (Belgium, Poland, Spain, Italy, Ireland) as obtaining exchange into the corresponding class; for the other sixteen the class field is null, meaning NOT RECORDED rather than not matched. Test requirements are null throughout for the same reason: the proviso buys exemption from part of the driving test and the title does not say which part. Chile is carried as a row but is NOT a beneficiary — 고시 630 suspended the agreement in 2007 and no resumption instrument exists in the category, so painting it would show a live treaty that is not one, while dropping it would assert an absence the register does not support. Vietnam and Sweden are excluded outright: their instruments are international-driving-permit arrangements, not domestic licence recognition.

agreements.name: RTA Dubai exchange list (Emirate of Dubai)
agreements.instrument: RTA service "Apply for a New Driving Licence or a New Category Based on Exchanging Licences", serviceId=121 ("Other Countries" variant), published service card; page states "Updated on: 22-July-2026". The sibling serviceId=122 is the separate Singapore variant.
agreements.basis: RTA publishes and amends the "exception countries" list itself, as a service card of the Dubai Licensing Agency; no counterparty, no instrument and no application by the foreign state appears anywhere in the chain, which is what makes it unilateral rather than the Danish shape (where a counterparty applies but still concludes nothing). AUTHORITY IS EMIRATE-LEVEL: UAE licences are issued by each emirate, this is Dubai’s list, and the federal Ministry of Interior page sits behind an F5 challenge that could not be read — so the beneficiaries paint what Dubai grants, not what the UAE grants. THE NATIONALITY GATE IS ON THE ROWS, NOT HERE: 35 of the 60 origins are open only to that country’s own nationals, so a painted beneficiary is not a promise to whoever holds the licence.
agreements.residence_condition: RTA states the eligible category as "Residents with a valid Driving Licence issued in one of the countries eligible for exchange", and the Service Requirements for "Exchange Licence - Resident with Dubai visa" are a valid Emirates ID, a valid electronic eye test and the original licence. A resident whose residence visa was issued by another emirate is served under "Exchange Licence - Resident with visa issued in another emirate", which additionally requires a copy of the trade licence for the Dubai branch and an employment verification letter; the FAQ answers that such an applicant may exchange in Dubai "provided that your company has a branch in Dubai", and otherwise "can exchange your licence in the emirate where your residence is issued". No minimum prior-residence period is published.

agreements.name: Italian reciprocity accords for licence conversion (art. 136 CdS)
agreements.instrument: Accordi di reciprocità per la conversione delle patenti di guida estere (art. 136 Codice della Strada, D.Lgs. 285/1992); condizioni di decadenza fissate dalla circolare prot. 31762 del 24 ottobre 2023
agreements.basis: The ministry states the condition of the list in terms: "Ciò è possibile se lo Stato che ha rilasciato l'abilitazione alla guida ha sottoscritto accordi di reciprocità con l'Italia" — each listed state has a reciprocity accord with Italy, several with printed expiry dates and renewal terms ("nuovo accordo valido dal 5 aprile 2026 al 4 aprile 2031"), which is a counterparty and an instrument rather than a domestic annex. BENEFICIARIES EXCLUDE THE FOUR RESTRICTED ROWS: Canada, Chile, the United States and Zambia convert only for diplomatic and consular staff, their families, or citizens on government mission, and painting them would show a general arrangement that Italy expressly does not grant. Two listed accords (El Salvador, Uruguay) print expiry dates already past while the states remain on the convertible list; they are carried as the ministry publishes them.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must be resident in Italy, and the foreign licence must have been obtained BEFORE acquiring Italian residence. A non-EU/EEA licence may be used in Italy for one year from acquisition of residence; after that year the licence must be converted to keep driving.

agreements.name: Norwegian exchange scheme for licences from outside the EU/EEA
agreements.instrument: Statens vegvesen — Innbytte av førerkort fra land utenfor EU/EØS (national exchange scheme; the eligible origins are enumerated by the authority, not by treaty)
agreements.basis: Statens vegvesen enumerates the eligible origins itself, on its own service pages, and states that anything not named cannot be exchanged. No counterparty, no application by the foreign state and no instrument appears anywhere in the chain, which is the Austrian and Dutch shape rather than the Irish one. THE ANNEX IS NOT UNIFORM: eight of the twelve origins are exchanged only after passing both the Norwegian theory and practical tests, so a painted beneficiary here is a right to APPLY, not a right to a licence without examination — read the rows.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must have fast bopel (settled residence) in Norway, documented by a bostedsattest from Skatteetaten. If the licence was obtained while the holder was registered as resident in Norway, the holder must show either that they had fast bopel in the issuing country when it was issued, or that it was obtained during a temporary stay abroad lasting at least six months. Full førerrett is required on moving to Norway and valid førerrett when applying.

agreements.name: Swedish exchange list for non-EEA licences (Transportstyrelsen)
agreements.instrument: Transportstyrelsen — Byta ut körkort från Förenade kungariket, Färöarna, Japan eller Schweiz
agreements.basis: Transportstyrelsen names four origins and states that no other non-EEA licence may be exchanged. There is no counterparty anywhere in the chain — the authority sets and publishes the list — which is the Dutch and Austrian shape. NOTHING IS RECORDED ABOUT TESTS: the page enumerates a procedure with no examination step but never states that a test is not required, so all four rows carry null on both test fields and no_retest is false on all four. A reader who wants "no test" from this list will not find it here, because the authority did not say it.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must be permanently resident in Sweden (permanent bosatt i Sverige), hold a valid licence, and meet the personal and medical requirements applying to a Swedish licence.

agreements.name: Traficom list of contracting and equated states
agreements.instrument: Traficom — Ulkomaisen ajokortin vaihtaminen suomalaiseen ajokorttiin; list of "Sopimusvaltiot ja niihin rinnastettavat valtiot" (contracting states and states equated with them)
agreements.basis: Traficom compiles and publishes the list of "sopimusvaltiot ja niihin rinnastettavat valtiot" itself, and the phrase equates two different things — states that are party to a convention and states merely EQUATED with them — which no counterparty agreed to. The right runs on Finnish law, not on an instrument with any of the 115. THE PAINTED SET IS A RIGHT INSIDE A WINDOW: outside two years of permanent residence, an expired entitlement, or the BE/truck/bus classes, the same origins face a full theory and driving test.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must be permanently resident in Finland ("Jotta voit saada suomalaisen ajokortin, sinun tulee asua vakituisesti Suomessa"). A licence first obtained while already living in Finland cannot be exchanged, though one renewed abroad while living in Finland can.

agreements.name: Polish exchange condition under the ustawa o kierujących pojazdami
agreements.instrument: Ustawa z dnia 5 stycznia 2011 r. o kierujących pojazdami, art. 14 ust. 1 — consolidated text announced by Obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu z dnia 1 września 2025 r., Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1226
agreements.basis: TYPED AGAINST THE AUSTRIA PRECEDENT, NOT AS THE CONVENTIONS. The Geneva 1949 and Vienna 1968 conventions appear in art. 14 ust. 1 only to DEFINE which foreign documents escape the extra theory examination; the right to exchange is conferred by the Polish statute and administered by the starosta, with no counterparty and no obligation on any convention party. Austria was typed the same way for the same reason: FSG s.23 cites Paris 1930, Geneva 1955 and Vienna 1982, but those govern driving on a foreign licence as a visitor, not exchange. Recording this as a multilateral instrument would also have claimed a group of destinations Poland does not bind. The research batch proposed multilateral_instrument; this is a deliberate re-typing, and the two rows carry the convention distinction that matters.
agreements.residence_condition: Not recorded. Art. 14 of the ustawa o kierujących pojazdami is silent on residence; the general issuance conditions sit in art. 11, which was not read for this row.

agreements.name: Czech exchange of non-EU licences (Ministerstvo dopravy)
agreements.instrument: Ministerstvo dopravy — Výměna řidičského průkazu vydaného nečlenským státem EU, který svým provedením neodpovídá Úmluvám o silničním provozu (Ženeva 1949, Vídeň 1968)
agreements.basis: TYPED AGAINST THE AUSTRIA PRECEDENT, NOT AS THE CONVENTIONS. Vienna 1968 and Geneva 1949 appear here as a test of the DOCUMENT'S FORM — "svým provedením bude odpovídat požadavkům (vzoru řidičského průkazu)" — not as instruments binding a counterparty to accept Czech licences. The exchange is granted by Czech law and administered by the obecní úřad obce s rozšířenou působností. The three named exceptions (Japan, the Republic of Korea, the United Arab Emirates) are stated by the ministry alone, with no reciprocal instrument produced. The research batch proposed multilateral_instrument; this is a deliberate re-typing on the same ground as Poland.
agreements.residence_condition: Holder of a valid non-EU licence with trvalý pobyt in Czechia, or přechodný pobyt for more than 1 year, is OBLIGED to apply for exchange. Where trvalý pobyt is absent, documents proving obvyklé bydliště in Czechia must be produced.

agreements.name: Greek conversion procedures for third-country licences (KYA 24058/2653/2004)
agreements.instrument: ΚΥΑ 24058/2653/2004 (Β΄1119) «Καθορισμός όρων και προϋποθέσεων, διαδικασίας ... για τη μετατροπή, σε ελληνικές, αδειών οδήγησης που εκδόθηκαν από κράτη μη μέλη της Ε.Ε. ή από χώρες της τέως Σοβιετικής Ένωσης», as implemented through ministry procedures 02.10 and 02.11; π.δ. 51/2012 (Α΄101)
agreements.basis: A KYA — a joint ministerial decision — fixing the conditions on which Greece converts licences "που εκδόθηκαν από κράτη μη μέλη της Ε.Ε.", delivered through the ministry's own numbered procedures 02.10 and 02.11 and administered by the regional transport directorates. No counterparty, no reciprocal undertaking and no bilateral instrument appears anywhere in the chain, which is the Dutch and Danish shape rather than the Irish one; the research batch proposed bilateral_agreement, and this is a deliberate re-typing on that ground. SIX OF THE SEVEN ROWS ASSERT NOTHING ABOUT TESTS: only the Swiss procedure title carries the words "χωρίς θεωρητική εξέταση".
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must have συνήθης διαμονή (normal residence) in Greece, or have been a student or pupil in Greece for at least six months before applying. A non-Greek national must produce a residence document issued at least 185 days before the application. The applicant must hold no other Greek, EU/EEA or third-country licence.

agreements.name: Japanese 外免切替 (foreign licence conversion) and its exemption list
agreements.instrument: 外国免許からの切替え（外免切替）— 道路交通法第97条の２第３項 (confirmation of knowledge and skill) with 道路交通法施行令第34条の４第２項 (waiver of the statutory written and practical tests); list of exempted countries/regions published by the licensing authority
agreements.basis: The exemption list is published by the licensing authority under 道路交通法第97条の2第3項 and its 施行令; no counterparty, no application by a foreign state and no instrument appears in the chain, so it is the same shape as the Austrian and Dutch annexes. WHAT IS PAINTED IS THE EXEMPTION, NOT THE EXCHANGE: 施行令第34条の4第2項 opens the route to any foreign Class 1 licence, so the beneficiaries here are the origins that additionally escape the 知識確認 and 技能確認, and every other origin still converts after sitting them. THE UNITED STATES IS DELIBERATELY NOT PAINTED: Japan names seven states and Indiana, and forty-three states are outside the exemption — the rows carry the detail the map cannot.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must have an address in Japan and apply to the prefectural licensing centre for that address (警視庁 states 住所が東京都内の方). Foreign nationals must produce a 住民票 showing 特定事項 (residence status and period) unless they hold MOFA-issued identification. Separately, an origin-side condition: the applicant must have stayed in the issuing country/region for a cumulative three months or more AFTER obtaining the foreign licence, evidenced by passport entry/exit stamps.

agreements.name: Singapore Traffic Police conversion of a foreign driving licence
agreements.instrument: Traffic Police, "Singapore Driving Licence" — Conversion of Foreign Driving Licence to Singapore Driving Licence (administrative criteria and document schedule)
agreements.basis: A published Traffic Police service with administrative criteria and a document schedule, set and amended by the force alone; no counterparty and no instrument anywhere. WHAT IS PAINTED IS NOT A TEST WAIVER: the three named beneficiaries are origins for which the Traffic Police publish an extra document requirement, and the underlying route is open to any valid full foreign licence — on terms that include the Basic Theory Test for everyone. RTA Dubai runs a separate Singapore-only service (serviceId=122) in the other direction; the two are not the same arrangement and are not linked here.
agreements.residence_condition: Conversion is compulsory for Singapore citizens, permanent residents, foreigners residing in Singapore for more than 12 months, and foreigners residing under 12 months who are employed as drivers on a Work Permit or S Pass. The origin-side condition is documentary: "Supporting documents to prove 1-year residency in country of issuance of driving licence with a physical residency of at least 6 months in the said country", whose stated purpose is "To determine intention of stay in country is not solely to obtain a driving licence". PRs, pass holders and citizens whose foreign licence was obtained after they got that status must additionally prove a minimum 6-month stay within a 12-month period in the issuing country.

agreements.name: Hong Kong direct issue under Schedule 4, Cap. 374B
agreements.instrument: Road Traffic (Driving Licences) Regulations (Cap. 374B), Schedule 4 — direct issue of a Hong Kong full driving licence without test
agreements.basis: Schedule 4 of the Road Traffic (Driving Licences) Regulations (Cap. 374B) is Hong Kong subsidiary legislation, amended by the Commissioner for Transport's own process; no counterparty appears in the instrument and no reciprocal undertaking is published, which is the unilateral shape rather than the Irish one. It is the widest genuinely test-free list in the region, and the one that asks least of the applicant on the destination side: there is no Hong Kong residence requirement at all.
agreements.residence_condition: No Hong Kong residence requirement for direct issue. The Transport Department expressly contemplates applicants living outside Hong Kong ("If you reside outside Hong Kong, you may fill in your non-Hong Kong residential address in the application form"), requiring only proof of present address plus a Hong Kong correspondence address. The residence test is on the ORIGIN side and is disjunctive: the licence was issued during a period of residence of not less than 6 months in the issuing place, OR it has been held for not less than 5 years immediately before the application, OR the applicant holds a passport or equivalent travel document of the issuing place.

agreements.name: Taiwan exchange without examination under 道路交通安全規則 art. 50
agreements.instrument: 道路交通安全規則 第50條第5項及第6項 (Regulations Governing Road Traffic Safety, Article 50(5)-(6))
agreements.basis: Article 50(5)-(6) of the 道路交通安全規則 is a domestic regulation of the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, applied by the motor vehicle offices; the reciprocity principle it invokes is a condition Taiwan applies to itself, not an instrument concluded with a counterparty, and the operative country list is administrative. THE PAINTED BENEFICIARIES ARE THE THREE PLACES THE PROVISION NAMES (the mainland area, Hong Kong and Macao). Every other foreign government sits behind 平等互惠原則 on a list that no official host would serve, so the layer carries one open row rather than a country list it could not read.
agreements.residence_condition: The applicant must hold proof of permitted stay or residence of six months or more (經許可停留或居留六個月以上之證明), and may apply from the day after entry (得於入境之翌日起). Nationals of the Republic of China with household registration in Taiwan produce a national identity card or military identity card instead.

agreements.name: Turkish exchange of foreign licences (Karayolları Trafik Yönetmeliği m.88)
agreements.instrument: NVİ, "Sürücü Belgeleri Hizmetleri Sıkça Sorulan Sorular", item (4) — documents required to exchange a driving licence obtained abroad. The rule it implements is Karayolları Trafik Yönetmeliği m.88 (heading and text as amended RG 17/04/2015-29329 and RG 05/06/2020-31146; original RG 18/07/1997-23053 mükerrer).
agreements.basis: The right runs on a Turkish regulation applied by NVİ at any nüfos müdürlüğü, with no annex of qualifying states and no counterparty in the general route; the three named bilaterals (Spain, Tunisia, the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus) sit alongside it under the article's own saving clause rather than constituting it. THE CLOCK IS THE OTHER WAY ROUND FROM EVERY OTHER ROW IN THIS LAYER: six months from the date of ENTRY during which the foreign licence may still be driven on, after which exchange is compulsory. NOTHING IS RECORDED ABOUT TESTS on any of the four rows, because neither the regulation nor the document list addresses them.
agreements.residence_condition: Karayolları Trafik Yönetmeliği m.88 keys the obligation to the date of entry to Türkiye rather than to residence; m.92 extends the same exchange rules to foreign nationals resident on a residence permit, stateless persons and accredited foreign staff, while barring them from driving Turkish-registered vehicles for gain.

agreements.name: Alberta-recognized jurisdictions (Alberta Transportation and Economic Corridors)
agreements.instrument: Exchange a licence from outside Alberta — Alberta-recognized jurisdictions; Operator Licensing and Vehicle Control Regulation (Traffic Safety Act)
agreements.basis: Alberta publishes the list as "Alberta-recognized jurisdictions" and describes the origins as jurisdictions it holds agreements with, and the reciprocity is visible from the other side inside this corpus: Germany lists Alberta in Anlage 11 FeV and the Netherlands lists Alberta on the RDW annex. The agreement paints no destination — Alberta has no ISO of its own, and painting Canada would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must provide proof of residence in Alberta and proof of legal status in Canada, and must be living in Alberta permanently — temporary residents (students, visitors, Seasonal Agricultural Worker Program workers) cannot get an Alberta licence.

agreements.name: ICBC licence exchange jurisdictions (British Columbia)
agreements.instrument: Moving from outside Canada — licence exchange jurisdictions
agreements.basis: ICBC administers the exchange under the Motor Vehicle Act and publishes a list of exchange jurisdictions; Germany lists British Columbia in Anlage 11 FeV, so the reciprocity is visible from the other side. THE LIST IS THE WEAKEST-SOURCED IN THIS BATCH: it ships in an RSC payload the quote gate strips, so the verified quote establishes the regime and the 90-day rule but not the membership. The agreement paints no destination — B.C. has no ISO of its own.
agreements.residence_condition: ICBC states you need to be a B.C. resident to apply for or hold a B.C. driver’s licence; tourists, exempt students and people ordinarily resident outside B.C. are outside the regime.

agreements.name: Ontario licence exchange agreements (Ministry of Transportation)
agreements.instrument: Exchange an out-of-province driver’s licence — licence exchange agreements
agreements.basis: Ontario publishes "licence exchange agreements" and names the jurisdictions it holds them with; Germany lists Ontario in Anlage 11 FeV, so the arrangement is visible from the other side. WHAT IS PAINTED IS AN EXCHANGE ROUTE, NOT A TEST WAIVER: all twenty-two rows are null on both test fields because the ministry ties the outcome to proven driving experience rather than to the jurisdiction. The agreement paints no destination — Ontario has no ISO of its own, and painting Canada would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: As of 11 May 2026 an applicant for a class G or class M licence must declare that Ontario is their primary place of residence and that their presence in Canada is legal.

agreements.name: Connecticut DMV out-of-country licence transfer (special situations)
agreements.instrument: Transfer Your Out-of-State License to CT — Special situations
agreements.basis: Connecticut DMV names Canada, Germany and France as the out-of-country licences it will transfer under its ordinary out-of-state process, and Germany lists Connecticut in Anlage 11 FeV — which is also the row that records a theory test on the German side, so the reciprocity is real without being symmetric in its terms. The agreement paints no destination: Connecticut has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Applies to new Connecticut residents transferring a licence; full-time students keeping an out-of-country permanent residence, active-duty military and visitors on a visitor’s visa are not required to transfer.

agreements.name: Delaware DMV reciprocity agreements (Class D)
agreements.instrument: Driver License Transfer (18 and over)
agreements.basis: Delaware DMV states the arrangement as a "reciprocity agreement" with three named states and sets it against the general rule that every other foreign licence sits both exams; Germany lists Delaware in Anlage 11 FeV, so the arrangement is visible from the other side. The agreement paints no destination: Delaware has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Page states: "Sixty days after the non-resident driver becomes a Delaware resident, he/she must apply for a Delaware driver license."

agreements.name: Georgia DDS reciprocal agreements (drivers from other nations)
agreements.instrument: Drivers From Other Nations
agreements.basis: Georgia DDS describes the origins as countries "that have a reciprocal agreement with the Georgia DDS" and names the consular certification the Korean route requires. The two rows are deliberately unequal: Korea's test waiver is stated, Taiwan's is not, and the layer records that difference rather than levelling it. The agreement paints no destination: Georgia has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Drivers with foreign licences do not need a Georgia licence unless they become a resident of Georgia.

agreements.name: Indiana BMV Reciprocal Driver's License Agreement
agreements.instrument: Residents with Out-of-Country Licenses — Reciprocal Driver’s License Agreement with Foreign Countries
agreements.basis: The BMV states it "has an agreement with the following countries for the reciprocal exchange of driver's licenses" and names Japan and Taiwan; Germany lists Indiana in Anlage 11 FeV on the same knowledge-test-required footing, and Japan separately names Indiana among its own exemptions — the two lists meet on this state from both sides. The agreement paints no destination: Indiana has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Applies to residents holding an out-of-country licence who wish to obtain an Indiana licence; applicant must be 18 or older for the skills-exam waiver.

agreements.name: Kentucky Division of Driver Licensing reciprocity countries
agreements.instrument: Non-U.S. Citizen Driver Licensing — Step One: Testing
agreements.basis: Kentucky names Taiwan and South Korea as reciprocity countries in both of its testing tables, which establishes the arrangement; what the same page cannot establish is what it does to the tests, because it says two incompatible things. Germany lists Kentucky in Anlage 11 FeV, so the reciprocity itself is visible from the other side. The agreement paints no destination: Kentucky has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Page states "A Kentucky license is required within 30 days of establishing Kentucky residency."

agreements.name: Louisiana OMV reciprocal agreements (out-of-country transfers)
agreements.instrument: OMV License Transfers — Transferring an Out-of-Country Driver’s License
agreements.basis: The OMV states the exemption as arising "due to a reciprocal agreement with the Department" and names four foreign states. Louisiana is the one US state with its own Swiss instrument in the SR 0.741.531 series — this corpus already carries it on the Swiss row as a sub-national partner — so the arrangement is documented from both ends, and Germany lists Louisiana in Anlage 11 FeV as well. The agreement paints no destination: Louisiana has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must be establishing Louisiana residency; visitors to the United States are not eligible for a Louisiana driver’s licence.

agreements.name: Oregon DMV testing waiver for new residents
agreements.instrument: Get a Driver License (testing waiver for new Oregon residents)
agreements.basis: ODOT names five foreign origins whose licences are transferred without a knowledge or drive test and states the contrasting rule for every other country on the same page. Germany lists Oregon in Anlage 11 FeV and Japan names Oregon among the seven US states in its own exemption list, so this state is documented from both sides twice over. The agreement paints no destination: Oregon has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Waiver applies to a person "new to Oregon" who surrenders the foreign licence.

agreements.name: Vermont DMV foreign driver's licence reciprocity (Taiwan)
agreements.instrument: Foreign Driver’s License Reciprocity
agreements.basis: The Vermont DMV states that it "has a reciprocal agreement for driver licensing with Taiwan" and waives the knowledge and skills tests for Class D on that footing. One row, one named counterparty, and no inference beyond it. The agreement paints no destination: Vermont has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Proof of Vermont residency and proof of lawful status in the United States are required; applicant must be at least 18.

agreements.name: Virginia DMV foreign licence exchange (form DL 7 reciprocity)
agreements.instrument: Exchange a Foreign Driver’s License (form DL 7)
agreements.basis: Virginia DMV publishes a list of countries with "reciprocal" status and states the evidential test it applies to grant it. Germany lists Virginia in Anlage 11 FeV and Japan names Virginia among the seven US states in its own exemption list, so this state is documented from both sides. The agreement paints no destination: Virginia has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must meet Virginia’s residency and identity requirements for a driver’s licence or driver privilege card; applicants under 18 are not eligible to exchange.

agreements.name: Wisconsin DOT foreign driver licence reciprocity
agreements.instrument: Foreign driver license reciprocity
agreements.basis: Wisconsin DOT states that it "has reciprocal agreements for driver licensing with these countries" and names four; Germany lists Wisconsin in Anlage 11 FeV, so the arrangement is visible from the other side. The age and experience floor is part of the agreement's terms, not a general Wisconsin rule, and is recorded in the notes rather than inferred away. The agreement paints no destination: Wisconsin has no ISO of its own, and painting the United States would claim a federal arrangement that does not exist.
agreements.residence_condition: Proof of Wisconsin residency and proof of legal presence in the United States are required; applicant must be at least 21 with 3 years of driving experience.

agreements.name: ANSV agreements on reciprocal recognition and exchange of driving licences
agreements.instrument: Bilateral agreements on reciprocal recognition and exchange of driving licences listed by the ANSV ('Consulta sobre los Acuerdos Internacionales de Licencias de Conducir'); the domestic licence framework is Ley 24.449 / Licencia Nacional de Conducir
agreements.basis: The ANSV publishes five named bilateral instruments ("Acuerdo entre Argentina y Bolivia sobre Reconocimiento y Canje de Licencias de Conducir", and four more) and administers the exchange centrally; each names a counterparty and each is titled as a reciprocal instrument, which is the Spanish and Irish shape rather than the Dutch one. What is painted is the five counterparties, and the Colombian row is an equivalence route rather than a canje — carried as its own row so the difference survives.
agreements.residence_condition: Holder must be resident in Argentina and hold a foreign licence that was valid and issued BEFORE residence was obtained (Chile and Bolivia pages). The Chile page requires the application within the first year of residence; the Colombia page states 'El trámite debe realizarse dentro de los 365 días desde la adquisición de la condición de residente en el territorio argentino.'

agreements.name: Resolução CONTRAN 933/2022 (exchange of a foreign licence)
agreements.instrument: Resolução CONTRAN nº 933, de 28 de março de 2022 (DOU 01/04/2022, Seção 1, p. 122), issued under art. 142 of the Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (Lei nº 9.503/1997)
agreements.basis: A CONTRAN resolution issued under art. 142 of the Código de Trânsito Brasileiro, amended and revoked by CONTRAN alone; the conventions and agreements art. 142 mentions determine which licences are RECOGNISED, but the exchange route itself — including the one for licences Brazil does not recognise — is domestic and open. NOTHING IS PAINTED AS A BENEFICIARY, because the instrument names no state: the two rows are classes of licence, not countries, and the SENATRAN list that would populate them could not be located.
agreements.residence_condition: Regular stay (estada regular) in Brazil. Under art. 2 §4, a driver whose foreign licence is recognised by Brazil (convention/agreement/reciprocity) who wishes to keep driving after 180 days of regular stay must obtain a CNH by passing the physical/mental aptitude exam and the psychological assessment. Under art. 3, a holder of a licence NOT recognised by Brazil may, while in regular stay, swap it for the Brazilian equivalent at the state/DF transit authority.

agreements.name: Ley de Tránsito art. 15 (licences for residents holding a foreign licence)
agreements.instrument: DFL Nº 1 de 2007 (Ministerio de Transportes y Telecomunicaciones), Fija texto refundido, coordinado y sistematizado de la Ley de Tránsito Nº 18.290 — art. 15 (originally art. 14 bis of Ley 18.290)
agreements.basis: A national statute (DFL Nº 1 de 2007 consolidating Ley 18.290) administered by municipal transit departments, open to every resident holding a foreign licence with no counterparty and no country list anywhere in the provision. NOTHING IS PAINTED: there are no named beneficiaries to paint, which is the accurate depiction of an open route — the alternative would have been to invent the list the statute deliberately does not have.
agreements.residence_condition: Must be a resident in Chile ('los residentes en Chile') holding a foreign licence; the licence is granted by the municipality of the applicant's comuna of residence.

agreements.name: Ley 9078 art. 91(b) — homologación of a foreign licence
agreements.instrument: Ley N.º 9078, Ley de Tránsito por Vías Públicas Terrestres y Seguridad Vial, artículo 91 ("Homologación de las licencias expedidas en el extranjero"), inciso b), publicada en La Gaceta, Alcance N.º 165 de 26 de octubre de 2012
agreements.basis: A statute of the Asamblea Legislativa administered by MOPT/Cosevi, open to any valid foreign licence on proof of lawful residence; no counterparty, no reciprocity condition and no annex. NOTHING IS PAINTED: an open route has no beneficiary list, and manufacturing one from the states whose licences happen to be common in Costa Rica would be the exact error this field exists to avoid.
agreements.residence_condition: Uninterrupted stay in Costa Rica of more than three months, and proof of lawful residence under immigration law ("Acreditar su permanencia legal en el país, al amparo de la legislación migratoria vigente")

agreements.name: ATTT homologación de licencia, and the Spain–Panama convenio
agreements.instrument: Trámite de "Homologación de licencia" (ATTT/SERTRACEN); requirements cite Ley 146 de 15 de abril de 2020 and article 113 acápite b.1 of the reglamento de tránsito
agreements.basis: The homologación route is a domestic procedure under Ley 146 de 2020 and art. 113 of the reglamento de tránsito, open to any foreign licence with no counterparty; the Spain row rides a separate convenio and is carried as its own row so the two are not merged. SPAIN IS THE ONLY PAINTED BENEFICIARY, and it is painted for the canje route rather than for the universal one — the universal route has no beneficiary list to paint, which is what makes it universal.
agreements.residence_condition: Foreign applicants must present an original carné de migración (or cédula E for permanent residents) plus passport; foreigners on temporary residence get a licence valid until the carné de migración expires or up to four years

agreements.name: Uruguayan canje (treaty route) and revalida (general route)
agreements.instrument: gub.uy trámite 'Canje de permiso de conducir extranjero de países con convenio - Canelones' (treaty route) and 'Revalida de permiso de conducir extranjero - Canelones' (general route)
agreements.basis: The quoted instrument is the treaty route — a canje for the holders of permits from "países con convenio", of which exactly one is currently in force — so the kind is recorded from what creates the entry, as it is for Ireland. The second row is candidly a unilateral domestic conversion and says so in its own note. SPAIN IS THE ONLY PAINTED BENEFICIARY: Italy's treaty expired in 2019 and painting it would show a live instrument that is not one, and the revalida route names no states at all.
agreements.residence_condition: Applicant must hold a Uruguayan identity document (cédula de identidad) or a valid Uruguayan passport, and must surrender any Uruguayan licences already held. No separate minimum-residence period is stated.
